papers.abstract: Biosecurity screening of synthetic DNA orders is a key defense against malicious actors and careless enthusiasts producing dangerous pathogens or toxins. It is important to evaluate biosecurity screening tools for potential vulnerabilities and to work responsibly with providers to ensure that vulnerabilities can be patched before being publicly disclosed. We consider a class of potential vulnerabilities in which a DNA sequence is obfuscated by splitting it into two or more fragments within a single synthetic DNA order, where the fragments can be readily reassembled via routine biological mechanisms. To evaluate this potential vulnerability, we develop a test set of obfuscated sequences based on controlled toxins, and share these materials with the biosecurity screening community. We then collect and analyze results from open-source and commercial biosecurity screening tools, alongside a novel Gene Edit Distance algorithm specifically designed to be robust against splitting-based obfuscations.

papers.abstract: Elucidating the failure mechanisms of Li metal electrodes is critical to accelerating the development of long cycle life Li metal batteries. However, it has not yet fully been realized so far due to the challenges associated with quantitative and qualitative characterization of solid electrolyte interphase on metal at large-area scale. Herein, we establish a relationship between solid byproducts and dead Li amounts in solid electrolyte interphase on Li metal by using fluorescence imaging and fluorescence titration method. The success of this methodology depends on the finding of a highly selective molecular probe, dilithium 3-hydroxy-2-naphthoate, with reversible change in fluorescence wavelength and intensity toward Li metal. Accordingly, the continuous generation of solid byproducts is acknowledged as potential underlying reason towards dead Li accumulation, determining the failure of Li electrode. These findings provide insights into the understanding of failure mechanism of Li metal electrode and design of strategies to improve its cycle life.

papers.abstract: The type VI secretion system (T6SS) is a large macromolecular complex crucial for inter-bacterial competition. Its expression and localization are tightly regulated, with the anti-bacterial H1-T6SS in Pseudomonas aeruginosa assembling in response to membrane damage. While several proteins are known to regulate this response, the mechanism remains unknown. Here, we use biochemical approaches to show formation of a complex between the membrane lipoprotein TagQ and the periplasmic protein TagR. Furthermore, Co-IP and in silico modeling indicates TagQ/R complex interactions with PpkA, likely dimerizing the kinase to initiate a phosphorylation cascade leading to H1-T6SS assembly. Mass spectrometry analysis of phosphorylated proteins in P. aeruginosa shows that PpkA does not have any targets outside of the previously reported Fha1, suggesting the sensor module acts exclusively to regulate T6SS assembly. Our work reveals the functional basis of the TagQR-PpkA signaling pathway and links membrane damage to localized H1-T6SS assembly, which is critical for efficient retaliation during inter-bacterial interactions.

papers.abstract: Polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures hold promise for high-density, energy-efficient nanoelectronics, but their controlled motion remains elusive due to strong pinning and lattice-coupled dynamics. Here, we report real-time observation of vortex boundary motion in PbTiO₃/SrTiO₃ heterostructures using localized trailing electric fields applied via a conductive atomic force microscopy (AFM) tip. The vortex boundaries show reversible motion that depends on both field polarity and AFM tip trajectory. By precisely steering the tip along specific paths, we achieve controlled, reconfigurable vortex boundary motion with remarkable stability over extended periods. In-situ scanning transmission electron microscopy further confirmed the controlled motion of the vortex boundary. Phase-field simulations reveal that this motion is governed by switching of the zigzag pattern at the vortex core, pinpointing the underlying physical mechanism. These results establish the feasibility of externally controlled vortex boundary motion, advancing both fundamental understanding of polar topological dynamics and prospects for next-generation polar-vortex-based nanoelectronic devices.

papers.abstract: Breeding wheat varieties with a high nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) reduces both production costs and threats to the ecological environment. Here, using candidate-gene and genome-wide association studies, we identify TaNPF7.6-A1 as a positive regulator of NUE in wheat. A widely conserved polymorphism in the coding region of TaNPF7.6-A1 produces allele TaNPF7.6-A1mod with a higher transcription level and nitrate transport activity than TaNPF7.6-A1lan, resulting in a greater NUE. We also reveal the mechanism by which TaEIL3-TaJAZ1-TaNPF7.6-A1 regulates NUE in wheat. TaNPF7.6-A1mod interacts more strongly with TaJAZ1 than TaNPF7.6-A1lan and promotes the retention of nuclear-localized TaJAZ1 in the cytoplasm. TaJAZ1 interacts with TaEIL3 and represses TaEIL3, binding to the TaNPF7.6-A1mod promoter, influencing allele expression and causing phenotypic differences. TaNPF7.6-A1mod also shows significant geographical distribution aggregation globally and undergoes continuous positive selection during the breeding process. Overall, this study provides molecular and evolutionary insights into the regulation of NUE.

papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) govern diverse cellular responses and are crucial drug targets. However, the sequence of structural events from G protein recognition to GDP release has remained elusive. Here, we leveraged the viral chemokine GPCR US28 to capture multiple activation states of the US28-Gq complex. Using cryo-electron microscopy and an engineered chemokine superagonist, we determined three distinct complex structures, capturing a GDP-bound Encounter state, the nucleotide-free Canonical state, and a putative intermediate bridging the two states, the Transition-to-Canonical state. These structures, along with simulations and functional data, provide high-resolution snapshots of a plausible G protein activation trajectory and support a stepwise conformational model for G protein activation. This activation cascade closely parallels mechanisms proposed for human GPCRs, suggesting a conserved GPCR signaling mechanism.

papers.abstract: Despite their significance, the genetic and molecular bases of neurodevelopmental disorders remain poorly understood. In this study, using human brain organoids and mouse models, we show that loss of NDE1, a gene closely associated with microcephaly, disrupts progenitor identity, prolongs mitosis, and alters regional patterning in the forebrain. NDE1 knockout leads to a caudal identity shift of neural progenitor cells in the organoids and mouse brains, coinciding with aberrant ERK signaling. Notably, downstream activation of the ERK pathway restored rostral PAX6 expression in human brain organoids. Parallel analyses of Nde1 knockout mice confirmed disrupted regional patterning of the forebrain. Together, our data establish NDE1 as a critical regulator of early human brain regionalization and elucidate molecular mechanisms underlying the structural abnormalities observed in NDE1-associated microcephaly.

papers.abstract: Piezoelectric surface acoustic wave devices can drive charge carriers in semiconductors through the acoustoelectric effect, generating direct currents with potential applications in sensing and biomedicine. However, current sources based on this mechanism that combine nanoampere-level precision, a wide dynamic range, and long-term operational stability have yet to be demonstrated. Here, we demonstrate an acoustically driven current source based on an InSb heterostructure integrated with a piezoelectric substrate. The output current is tunable from 1.22 nA to 25.46 μA by adjusting the input radio-frequency power, with a sensitivity down to the nanoampere scale. At an input power of 10 mW, the device delivers an average output current of 1.54 μA with 1% accuracy and maintains a standard deviation of 4.82 nA over 12 h of continuous operation. Its acoustic-to-electrical conversion efficiency can be further enhanced by implementing multiple interdigital transducer arrays and single-phase unidirectional transducer structures, enabling cooperative excitation and directional acoustic energy propagation. The device also supports wireless excitation and accelerates wound healing in a rat full-thickness skin defect model under low-intensity electrical stimulation. These results establish a wireless acoustoelectric platform for stable, tunable, and miniaturized current delivery, suggesting potential for biomedical applications.

papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment landscape for many cancers, but fails to improve the outcomes of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), in which low tumor antigen presentation restricts the recognition and eradication of cancerous cells by immunocytes. We here report an approach to in situ reprogramming hypoimmunogenic glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) into type 1 conventional dendritic cell (cDC1)-like cells for presenting endogenous tumor antigens and priming sustained tumoricidal T-cell responses. Specifically, our cavity-injectable nucleobase-derived lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-hydrogel superstructure efficiently delivers transcription factors (PU.1, IRF8, BATF3) and the costimulatory molecule (TNFSF9) into GSCs to induce cDC1-like reprogramming. These cDC1-like cells potentiate GBM immunogenicity, elicit robust adaptive immunity and long-term antitumor memory, thereby inhibiting tumor growth and preventing postoperative GBM relapse in mice. Collectively, this work establishes in situ tumor cell reprogramming into licensed cDC1-like cells as a therapeutic paradigm for converting immunologically "cold" tumors into a self-vaccinating immune niche with broad translational potential for hypoimmunogenic malignancy treatment.

papers.abstract: As sharing the anatomical entrance to the larynx, swallowing plays not only an important role in food and water intake, but also a major role in defensive mechanism for preventing the risk of foreign matter aspiration. Besides water/acid, the mechanical stimulation of food or foreign matter could induce swallowing, yet the relevant sensory pathways remain poorly understood. Here, using male mice as a model, we clarify that vagal sensory neurons expressing Piezo2 responsibly transmit swallowing induced mechanical stimuli from the pharynx to tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH + ) neurons in the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS), then to ambiguus nucleus/rostral ventrolateral medulla (Amb/RVLM complex). Specific activation of Piezo2+ vagal sensory neurons or TH + NTS neurons can induce swallowing behavior. Either inhibition of TH + NTS neurons or Piezo2 knockout in vagal sensory neurons can abolish swallowing reflex. Notably, we elucidate that the TH + NTS-Amb/RVLM pathway serves as a shared downstream pathway for both mechanical and chemical stimuli-elicited swallowing. Collectively, we describe a pharynx-to-brain sensory pathway that provides a basis for central integration of swallowing and airway defensive reflexes.

papers.abstract: Our previous study revealed that Piezo1 in colonic goblet cells senses mechanical stimuli to regulate the production and secretion of MUC2, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Altered endoplasmic reticulum function and the unfolded protein response (UPR), which are critical for MUC2 protein folding and secretion, were observed in goblet cell-specific Piezo1 knockout mice. This study aimed to investigate whether and how Piezo1 in goblet cells modulates mucus barrier function by regulating the UPR. In vitro, LS174T cells were subjected to orbital shaking to simulate fluid shear stress (FSS) stimulation. The expression of UPR-related molecules and MUC2 was detected using real-time PCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining in the presence or absence of Piezo1 and UPR inhibition. In vivo, goblet cell-specific Piezo1 knockout (cKO) mice were treated with dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) and water avoidance stress (WAS). We analysed changes in goblet cell morphology, mucus layer thickness, UPR-related protein expression and ER structure. In addition, DSS-induced colitis mice were intraperitoneally injected with Yoda1 to activate Piezo1, and alterations in pathological structures and mucus layer thickness were subsequently evaluated. Compared with PERK or ATF6, FSS activated PIEZO1 and promoted calcium influx, thereby maintaining ER calcium homeostasis and selectively activating the IRE1α-XBP1 signalling pathway. This cascade facilitated MUC2 production, whereas pharmacological inhibition of PIEZO1 or IRE1α expression significantly abolished these effects. Compared with WT mice, cKO mice exhibited aggravated mucus barrier impairment, downregulated IRE1α-XBP1 and aggravated ER swelling under DSS and WAS. In contrast, pharmacological activation of Piezo1 via Yoda1 treatment restored intestinal mucus layer thickness and ameliorated colitis in DSS mice. Piezo1 senses mechanical stimulation to maintain ER calcium homeostasis and modulates the UPR via the IRE1α-XBP1 pathway, thereby facilitating MUC2 production in goblet cells and maintaining intestinal mucosal barrier homeostasis. Piezo1 in colonic goblet cells senses intestinal mechanical stimulation and modulates endoplasmic reticulum calcium homeostasis via Ca2+ influx. The Piezo1-Ca2+-IRE1α-XBP1 signaling axis controls Mucin2 synthesis and production to maintain intestinal mucus barrier integrity. Pharmacological activation of Piezo1 by Yoda1 rescues mucus barrier defects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for gastrointestinal mucosal injury.

papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients, yet PD-specific biomarkers and prediction models remain limited. This study aimed to identify glycated peptide biomarkers associated with CVD in PD patients and develop a prediction model integrating glycated proteomics and clinical indicators using machine learning. In Phase I, a matched discovery cohort (48 PD patients with CVD and 48 without CVD) was used to identify glycated peptides by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with glmnet used to prioritise candidate biomarkers. In Phase II, candidate biomarkers were quantified in a prospective internal derivation cohort (n = 240) and a multicentre external validation cohort (n = 102). The combined model was developed using F-test feature selection and elastic-net logistic regression. Its predictive performance was compared with three published cardiovascular risk models. Patients were stratified using a training-derived Youden cutoff. In the discovery cohort, 257 glycated peptides were differentially abundant between groups. Four candidate biomarkers were prioritised, and two peptides, GEAFTLK(g)ATVLNYLPK and K(g)QHLFVK, were retained in the final model together with six clinical indicators: phosphate, diabetes, total Kt/V, albumin, cardiac troponin T, and glycated albumin. The combined model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.784 in the training set, 0.781 in the internal testing set, and 0.822 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Using the training-derived cutoff of 0.373, higher 1-year CVD incidence was observed in the high-risk group in both validation cohorts. The combined model also achieved higher ROC-AUCs than the published cardiovascular risk models. We developed and externally validated a PD-specific CVD prediction model by integrating glycated peptide biomarkers with clinical indicators, which may facilitate earlier risk stratification and targeted prevention.

papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), remains a leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Therapeutic resistance substantially limits the efficacy of chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy. For example, only approximately 30% of patients with HCC derive clinical benefit from sorafenib, and acquired resistance commonly develops within six months, underscoring the urgent need to clarify the molecular basis of treatment failure. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed RNA molecules with high structural stability and tissue-specific expression. In liver cancer, circRNAs regulate therapeutic resistance through multiple mechanisms that converge on ferroptosis suppression, apoptosis evasion, DNA damage repair, oncogenic signaling, immune escape, and cancer stemness. Beyond the canonical competing endogenous RNA model, this review highlights emerging regulatory mechanisms involving RNA-binding protein interactions, circRNA-encoded functional micropeptides, and circRNA-mediated phase separation. Exosomal circRNAs also facilitate the intercellular transmission of resistant phenotypes and remodel the tumor immune microenvironment. We systematically summarize circRNA-mediated resistance across different therapeutic modalities and critically evaluate the available evidence according to experimental models, in vivo validation, and patient validation. Although circRNAs show potential as biomarkers for predicting therapeutic response and as targets for overcoming resistance, most candidates remain at the preclinical stage. Their clinical translation is constrained by the lack of standardized detection methods, insufficient multicenter validation, and inefficient and inadequately targeted in vivo delivery systems. Because most direct mechanistic evidence is derived from HCC, selected iCCA-related findings are incorporated where available.

papers.abstract: Interactions between T cell receptors (TCRs), peptides, and human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) underlie antigen-specific T cell immunity. Despite substantial advances in prediction methods, accurate modeling of coupled TCR-peptide-HLA recognition remains underdeveloped, limiting applications such as TCR and neoepitope prioritization in cancer and antigen identification in autoimmunity. Here we present StriMap, a unified framework for predicting TCR-peptide-HLA interactions by integrating physicochemical, sequence-context, and structural features at recognition interfaces. StriMap achieves state-of-the-art performance with improved generalizability and enables applications in cancer and autoimmunity. As a case study, we screened 13 million peptides from 43,241 bacterial proteins and identified candidate molecular mimics that were experimentally validated to activate T cells expressing an ankylosing spondylitis (AS)-associated TCR. A top validated peptide was enriched in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), suggesting potential shared microbial triggers. Overall, StriMap provides a framework for rational immunotherapy design and dissecting antigenic drivers of autoimmunity.

papers.abstract: Prostate intraepithelial neoplasia (PIN) is a recognized precursor to prostate cancer (PCa) and shares many histological and molecular features with invasive disease. To clarify the relationship between PIN and PCa, we performed integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses on epithelial and stromal laser-capture microdissected samples in matched PIN (n = 121), PCa (n = 217), and adjacent normal (AN, n = 115) prostate tissue from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples across three datasets. We identified two epithelial and two stromal transcriptomic clusters, termed 'invasive-like' and 'normal-like', which were present across all datasets. Among PIN samples, 46% of epithelial and 38% of stromal samples were classified as invasive-like. Whole-genome sequencing analysis revealed recurrent copy number alterations in PIN and PCa lesions, with recurrent copy number alterations more frequently shared between invasive-like PIN and PCa. This study provides new insight into PIN biology and the relationship between PIN and invasive PCa and highlights a transcriptional signature in PIN samples that may have prognostic implications. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) has established itself as an essential post-treatment biomarker in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). While achieving undetectable MRD (uMRD) reliably predicts prolonged progression-free survival (PFS) for individual patients across clinical trials, establishing MRD as a universal, trial-level regulatory surrogate endpoint across contemporary targeted therapies remains a formidable biostatistical hurdle. This perspective addresses the "atomistic fallacy" underlying the apparent erosion of trial-level surrogacy observed in aggregate meta-analyses. We demonstrate that the attenuation of trial-level surrogacy stems from fundamental biological effect modification-specifically the distinction between cytostatic therapies (e.g., continuous Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors) and cytotoxic, deep-remission regimens (e.g., fixed-duration venetoclax combinations)-as well as operational confounders introduced by modern adaptive trial designs. Reconciling these individual- and trial-level observations requires transitioning from a binary endorsement model to a mechanism-dependent, context-specific framework for surrogate endpoint validation in CLL.

papers.abstract: Cancer therapies are commonly evaluated by target inhibition, pathway modulation, or initial tumor response, yet these measures do not reliably predict which treatments produce lasting disease control. Many pharmacodynamically active therapies produce transient benefit followed by relapse, while others achieve therapeutic durability despite comparable initial activity. This Perspective argues that durability is better explained by the behavior of the treated tumor system than by the depth of target suppression and distinguishes three modes of intervention behavior: buffered suppression, in which adaptive escape remains broadly accessible; adaptive constraint, in which future tumor states are narrowed without eradication; and collapse-dominant control, in which treatment drives a state transition that leaves few routes for persistence. Examples from targeted therapy, differentiation therapy, checkpoint blockade, and CAR-T therapy illustrate how the same modality can produce different intervention behaviors depending on tumor biology. A prospective sequence is also proposed for testing which behavior a candidate therapy is likely to induce.

papers.abstract: The revision of the WHO classification of CNS tumours now distinguishes grade 4 diffuse gliomas by their molecular features, but tailored treatment is yet to be standardised. Glioblastoma (isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH))-wildtype tumours harbouring an unmethylated O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase "(uMGMT)" promoter are inherently resistant to temozolomide (TMZ). However, no standardised treatment recommendations are available for grade 4 astrocytoma IDH-mutant. We previously demonstrated that administration of bortezomib (BTZ) 48 h prior to TMZ depletes MGMT protein and sensitizes uMGMT glioma cells to TMZ. Based on these findings, a phase IB/II trial was initiated to evaluate the safety and clinical activity of sequential BTZ and TMZ. This interim analysis aimed to determine a futility safeguard, identify molecular and pharmacodynamic determinants of treatment response and failure in the first 15 patients consecutively treated. Adult patients with recurrent grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma or IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, uMGMT promoter, measurable disease, Karnofsky Performance Status ≥ 70, and disease progression ≥ 12 weeks after radiotherapy were enrolled. Patients received intravenous BTZ 1.3 mg/m² on days 1, 4, and 7 of each 28-day cycle, followed by oral TMZ 200 mg/m²/day for 5 consecutive days beginning on day 3. Targeted sequencing of glioma-associated genes and longitudinal plasma proteomic profiling using LC-MS/MS were performed before, during, and after treatment. Fifteen patients (median age 52 years) comprised 10 patients with IDH- wildtype glioblastoma and 5 patients with grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma. Disease control (partial response and stable disease) was observed in 4/10 (40%) IDH- wildtype glioblastoma patients, comprising one PR and three cases of SD. In contrast, all five patients with grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma experienced rapid progressive disease. Notably, non-responding IDH-wildtype glioblastomas and all IDH-mutant tumours harboured alterations affecting the CDKN2A/RB1-cell-cycle regulatory axis, including CDKN2A and/or RB1loss, with one IDH-mutant patient additionally harbouring PIK3CA gain. By comparison, responding IDH-wildtype glioblastomas were characterized by amplified EGFR, nuclear NF-κB (p65/RelA) activation, and absence of RB-pathway alterations. Longitudinal proteomic analyses demonstrated comparatively attenuated treatment-induced changes in proteins associated with invasion and extracellular matrix remodelling in responders, whereas proteins involved in damage clearance immune phenotype, platelet activation, aggregation, and degranulation were significantly altered during disease control. Sequential BTZ and TMZ therapy was feasible with manageable hematologic and non-hematologic toxicities and met prespecified interim futility criteria, supporting continued recruitment to the phase II study. Disease control was restricted to a molecularly defined subset of IDH- wildtype glioblastoma characterized by EGFR amplification and NF-κB activation. In contrast, universal treatment failure among grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytomas was associated with alterations of the CDKN2A/RB1 cell-cycle checkpoint pathway, suggesting that advanced molecular evolution and cell-cycle deregulation may override the survival advantage typically associated with IDH-mutant gliomas and limit the effectiveness of MGMT-targeted sensitization strategies. ClinicalTrials.gov trial registration number: NCT03643549, date of registration: 2018-08-21.

papers.abstract: Acute allograft rejection is largely dependent on T cell-driven immune responses; however, the molecular programs that establish and maintain effector T cell states during rejection remain incompletely defined. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis was conducted to characterize the activation of signalling pathways in T cells during acute allograft rejection. The function of MEK1/2 signalling was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo using mice with targeted deletion of Mek1/2 in T cells and pharmacological inhibition. Phosphoproteomic analysis, immunofluorescence staining, and western blotting were conducted to investigate downstream signalling mechanisms, particularly those involving SMAD4. Effector CD4 and CD8 T cells exhibited enhanced MEK/ERK pathway activation throughout the rejection process. MEK1/2 inhibition, either via genetic deletion or pharmacological blockade, attenuated T cell activation and effector activity, leading to reduced rejection and prolonged graft survival. Phosphoproteomic analysis identified SMAD4 as a key downstream effector of MEK1/2 signalling. Mechanistically, MEK1/2 deficiency reduced SMAD4 nuclear translocation in activated T cells, accompanied by diminished effector T cell responses. MEK1/2 signalling regulates T cell activation and effector phenotypes via SMAD4 nuclear translocation in heart transplant rejection. Therapeutic intervention targeting this pathway may contribute to alloimmune response regulation and improve transplant outcomes.

papers.abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

papers.abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion are hallmarks of cancer metastasis, but how tumor metabolism shapes the immune microenvironment during colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis remains poorly understood. The role of E-cadherin (CDH1) beyond cell adhesion is unexplored. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, pseudotime trajectory inference, and in vivo/in vitro functional assays in primary and liver-metastatic CRC models. CellChat was used to map intercellular communication. Histone lactylation, ADAM10 activation, and CDH1 shedding were validated by biochemical and immunohistochemical assays. PGK1-driven glycolysis is upregulated in liver metastases and promotes metastatic progression. Elevated lactate induces histone H3K18 lactylation, activating ADAM10 expression. ADAM10 cleaves CDH1, releasing its soluble ectodomain. This fragment acts as a ligand for KLRG1 on T cells, driving exhaustion and immunosuppression. Cell-cell communication analysis confirmed CDH1-KLRG1 as a top differentially activated pathway in metastasis. Functionally, targeting PGK1 or blocking CDH1 shedding inhibits liver metastasis and restores T-cell function. We identify a metabolic-epigenetic-immune axis in which tumor glycolysis reprograms immunity via lactate-induced CDH1 shedding. Soluble CDH1 functions as an immunomodulatory signal, linking metabolic activity to T-cell exhaustion. This redefines CDH1 as a dual-function molecule and reveals actionable targets for metastatic CRC. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: The tumor-stroma percentage (TSP) has been proposed as a prognostic factor in ovarian cancer. When assessed manually by pathologists, the TSP can be subject to significant inter-rater variability. Automated methods for TSP determination have recently been developed. Existing approaches typically yield a single TSP value for a relatively small region of interest in the slide, introducing bias through region selection and potentially overlooking the TSP distribution across the entire histologically examined area. We present an adaptable deep learning pipeline, efficiently fine-tuned for ovarian cancer tissue analysis using a few-shot learning approach, requiring only minimal new training annotations. Instead of calculating a single TSP value, our method quantifies the global TSP distribution across the entire tumor and therefore captures its spatial heterogeneity. To identify a prognostic biomarker, we systematically evaluated a panel of metrics describing this distribution in 98 patients. Our analysis revealed that the mean-median difference of the TSP distribution [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.60, 95% CI = 0.46-0.79, p < 0.001], a quantitative measure of asymmetry, together with the mean TSP (HR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.43-0.97, p = 0.03), are biomarkers significantly associated with recurrence-free survival. By successfully adapting a pipeline for ovarian cancer, we demonstrate that automated analysis of the entire TSP distribution provides significant prognostic information superior to that obtained by manual assessment. Spatial heterogeneity of the TSP is a key prognostic factor. © 2026 Fraunhofer IIS and The Author(s). papers.abstract: The aims of the study were to elucidate the regulatory role of rhomboid family protein 2 (RHBDF2) in breast cancer chemoresistance and the underlying molecular mechanisms to provide a theoretical basis and research direction to facilitate the development of potential therapeutic interventions. Chemoresistance and apoptosis assays, and mouse tumor-bearing models were used to evaluate the correlation between RHBDF2 expression and breast cancer chemoresistance. Doxorubicin accumulation, rhodamine efflux, immunohistochemical staining, Western blot, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction were used to validate the regulatory relationships in protein expression and function for RHBDF2, MDR1 (ABCB1), and SEC62 (a critical component of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane insertion machinery). Immunofluorescence staining and immunoprecipitation assays were employed to determine the molecular mechanisms underlying RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis-mediated regulation of breast cancer chemoresistance. The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis constitutes the core regulatory pathway in breast cancer chemoresistance. When RHBDF2 is highly expressed, it binds to heat shock cognate protein 70 (HSC70), a central chaperone-mediated autophagy receptor, thereby blocking the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62, maintaining SEC62 protein levels, and promoting membrane integration of MDR1 to enhance drug resistance. Under downregulated RHBDF2 expression, the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62 increases, leading to impaired MDR1 function and substantially reduced cellular drug resistance. The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis is the core signaling pathway that governs chemoresistance in breast cancer. Targeted interventions against key molecules or related signaling nodes in this axis can provide a theoretical basis for developing novel therapeutic strategies to reverse chemoresistance, with great clinical translational value.

papers.abstract: Proficient mismatch repair colorectal cancer (pMMR-CRC) exhibits resistance to immunotherapy, presenting a significant clinical challenge that must be addressed. Exosomes, which serve as mediators of intercellular communication, play a crucial role in the tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the mechanisms that exosomes regulate tumor immunity in pMMR-CRC need to be fully elucidated. In this study, we discovered that circSENP5, a circular RNA (circRNA), is highly expressed in pMMR-CRC and is derived from exosomes that are transferred to tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). This transfer enhances the oxidative phosphorylation of macrophages and promotes immunosuppressive characteristics, as well as increased levels of inhibitory receptors on CD8+ T cells. Mechanistically, circSENP5 binds to the deubiquitinase USP10, stabilizing LRPPRC, a key regulator of mitochondrial function. This interaction protects LRPPRC from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, resulting in enhanced mitochondrial respiration and immune suppression. in vivo, the overexpression of circSENP5 accelerates tumor progression, while its mutation disrupts the interaction with USP10, leading to reduced TAM infiltration and improved CD8+ T cell function. Targeting circSENP5 in combination with anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint therapy effectively suppresses tumor progression, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy. These findings suggest that exosomal circSENP5 plays a pivotal role in immune evasion in pMMR-CRC by modulating mitochondrial metabolism in TAMs, thereby providing potential therapeutic targets for overcoming immune resistance in pMMR-CRC.

papers.abstract: Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

papers.abstract: Cardiac lymphatics regulate fluid homeostasis and immune cell clearance. The mechanisms underlying cardiac lymphatic vessel formation remain unclear. We perform spatial transcriptomics on the zebrafish heart at the single-cell level and investigate gene expression patterns in cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). adrenomedullin a (adma) is mainly expressed in the epicardium adjacent to cardiac lymphatics. adma mutants develop edema and dilated outflow tracts with mis-patterned and reduced lymphatics, while their ventricular lymphatics are dilated with fewer sprouts, increased lyve1b expression, and altered lymphatic subpopulation composition. Loss of ackr3a, which encodes an Adm decoy receptor, increases lymphatic sprouts. During heart regeneration, adma and ackr3a are expressed in epicardium-derived cells within the wound. Neutrophil clearance is reduced in adma mutants but increased in ackr3a mutants. Our findings uncover the heterogeneity of cardiac LECs and show that Adm and Ackr3 regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation in the zebrafish heart.

papers.abstract: How do inflammation and activation of the regenerative genetic program affect intestinal epithelial cell behavior and shape responses to future injuries? Following injury, which typically induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) death, regeneration occurs via the proliferation of surviving ISCs and via cellular plasticity through dedifferentiation of progenitors and committed cells. While inflammation and cellular plasticity are hallmarks of regeneration, its long-term effects on epithelial cell behavior are not well understood. Using single cell multiomics, we demonstrate that inflammatory exposure and cellular plasticity imprint a lasting transcriptional and epigenetic memory on ISCs and their progeny, priming them for enhanced repair after subsequent injuries. Mechanistically, we identify IFN-γ as a critical driver of this primed regenerative state. These findings uncover how prior inflammation reprograms regenerative capacity, with implications for tissue resilience and disease susceptibility.

papers.abstract: Uterine aging impairs fertility and reproductive health, but the underlying pathogenic mechanisms and effective treatment strategies remain elusive. Defective endometrial decidualization and implantation failure are hallmarks of uterine aging, which can be driven by cellular senescence, especially in endometrial stromal cells (EnSCs). Rb1 has been reported to relieve cellular senescence by suppressing oxidative and inflammatory pathways. However, whether Rb1 functions in alleviating uterine aging remains uncertain. Here, we demonstrate that Rb1 can attenuate oxidative stress, senescence, and apoptosis in the EnSCs of the aging human endometrium and murine uterus. Further proteomic analysis reveals that Rb1 safeguards against endometrial aging by regulating mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)-related pathways. Rb1 treatment results in the activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and AMPK-mediated suppression of the mTOR-nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling loop, thereby ameliorating aging-related phenotypes. Collectively, our findings illustrate that Rb1 alleviates uterine aging by attenuating endometrial stromal cell senescence and suppressing AMPK-mTOR-NF-κB-driven inflammatory signaling. Rather than selectively eliminating senescent cells, Rb1 primarily targets senescence-associated dysfunction and restores endometrial homeostasis, highlighting its potential as a senescence-modulating therapeutic strategy for uterine aging.

papers.abstract: Indigenous Peoples in Canada are disproportionately burdened with a spectrum of health issues and consistently report lower satisfaction with their health care; nevertheless, little is known about their experiences with critical care and the support received during critical illness. We aimed to describe the current scope of critical-care-specific resources available to Indigenous patients and their families across Alberta to identify gaps and opportunities to implement actionable change to realize more equitable and culturally safe care. We conducted a two-phase environmental scan. Phase 1 entailed searching websites for information to support Indigenous patients, their families, and health care workers. Phase 2 facilitated 21 interviews with intensive care unit (ICU) stakeholders from across Alberta to further describe site-specific resources, services, tools, or initiatives to support Indigenous Peoples. Indigenous partners were engaged through all aspects of the project. Our environmental scan identified a paucity of ICU-specific resources, programs, or policies to support Indigenous patients and families' navigation with critical care. We identified two national resources aimed at clinicians, rather than patients or families. Interviews with ICU stakeholders confirmed the paucity of Indigenous-specific resources. Stakeholders cited numerous barriers, including inadequate culture training, staff time constraints and burnout, physical space limits, and insufficient personnel, such as Indigenous liaisons and social workers. Multiple gaps exist in the availability of critical-care-focused resources and supports for Indigenous Peoples experiencing critical illness in Alberta, Canada. Addressing these care gaps may improve health equity, access, and the experience for Indigenous patients and families during critical illness and further build trust and strengthen relationships with health care workers.

papers.abstract: Pain after kidney transplantation is often severe, and graft function constrains the use of systemic analgesia. Previous syntheses of regional techniques pooled them as a class, combined donors with recipients, and did not use a minimal clinically important difference (MCID). We searched PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through 5 September 2026 for randomised trials of regional analgesia in adult kidney transplant recipients (PROSPERO CRD420261478933); a trial-registry search and network meta-analysis were added post hoc. Bayesian random-effects models with MCID-scaled priors yielded posterior probabilities of benefit and of exceeding the MCID, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework. Fourteen trials (903 participants) were included. Only quadratus lumborum (QL) and transversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks could be pooled against control. Both yielded lower pain at every pooled time point, but no pairwise pain comparison reached 80% probability of exceeding the 1.0 point MCID. Opioid consumption at 24 h was lower with the QL block (-15.5 morphine milligram equivalents; 95% credible interval -23.6 to -6.7) and the TAP block (-10.5; -14.4 to -5.5), with each reduction exceeding the 5 mg MCID with a probability >97%. In the network meta-analysis, no difference between QL and TAP blocks in pain or opioid consumption reached 80% probability of exceeding the MCID. Graft function and safety data were too sparse to pool. Twelve eligible registered trials were unpublished; certainty of evidence was very low. Quadrtus lumborum and transversus abdominus plane blocks reduce pain and opioid consumption at 24 h, but only the reduction in opioid consumption has a high probability of being clinically important. Certainty of evidence is very low; no technique is preferred, and effects on graft function are unknown.

papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease increasingly linked to T cell responses, although the mechanisms driving T cell activation and disease progression remain unclear. Here we used single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing, longitudinal immune profiling and imaging flow cytometry to identify long-lived intrathecal clonotypes and antigen-presenting cell-T cell complexes displaying features of immunological synapse formation, consistent with intrathecal antigen presentation. Higher frequencies of CD4+ effector, CD4+ regulatory and CD8+ T cells in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were associated with slower disease progression, whereas increased circulating CD4+ effector and regulatory T cells were associated with faster progression. T cell clonotypes shared between blood and CSF exhibited distinct transcriptional states. Finally, frequencies of cytomegalovirus-specific T cells in CSF and anticytomegalovirus serum antibodies were correlated with faster progression and shorter survival in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These findings reveal compartmentalized immune dynamics, largely contrasting protective intrathecal responses with harmful systemic activation.

papers.abstract: Objective: To assess the long-term oncologic and survival outcomes of percutaneous cryoablation (PCA) for patients with solitary de novo T1a renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Methods: This retrospective study was conducted following the STROBE guidelines. We included patients with a single, biopsy-confirmed, treatment-naïve T1a RCC (<4 cm) who underwent PCA between January 2008 and December 2021. Patient demographics, tumor characteristics, and procedural details were collected. Survival analyses were performed using the Kaplan-Meier estimator. Results: Eighty-six patients (57 men and 29 women) with a median age of 69 years met the inclusion criteria. Fifty patients (58%) had a history of an additional non-renal malignancy. In total, 86 renal tumors were treated using PCA, with a median tumor diameter of 2.7 cm. Clear cell RCC accounted for 67.4% of the tumors. Procedural complications classified as Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher occurred in 4.6% of cases. Local tumor recurrence at the ablation site was observed in five patients (5.8%), and four patients (4.6%) developed new lesions elsewhere within the kidney. The estimated median overall survival was 10.34 years. The 10-year local recurrence-free and disease-free survival rates were 93.5% and 84.0%, respectively. Both metastasis-free survival and cancer-specific survival rates at 10 years were 100%. Conclusions: Percutaneous cryoablation provided durable local tumor control with low major morbidity and favorable long-term oncologic outcomes in this selected cohort of patients with solitary cT1a renal tumors.

papers.abstract: Introduction: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based molecular residual disease (MRD) testing is emerging as a tool to refine relapse risk and guide surveillance after curative-intent therapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Tissue-free (plasma-only) MRD assays may improve feasibility where tumor tissue is limited. Prospective and trial-embedded studies have established that ctDNA MRD detected after curative-intent therapy is prognostic for recurrence in NSCLC, but how tissue-free MRD testing is deployed in routine care in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East (AMEA) has not been described. We characterized ordering patterns and first-test positivity in an AMEA cohort. In this descriptive cohort (159 NSCLC patients; 257 samples), 40.9% of patients underwent more than one MRD test, with a median interval of 4.9 months between the first two tests; first-test MRD positivity was 15.7% (25/159; 95% CI 10.9-22.2) with rates of 0% (0/9; 95% CI 0.0-29.9), 8.8% (5/57; 95% CI 3.8-18.9), 21.5% (17/79; 95% CI 13.9-31.8) and 21.4% (3/14; 95% CI 7.6-47.6), respectively, across stages I, II, III, and oligometastatic stage IV disease. No hypothesis testing was performed, and the stage I and oligometastatic stage IV subgroups are small, so the confidence intervals overlap widely and apparent between-stage differences should not be interpreted as a stage effect. Case Presentation: Six illustrative cases involving patients with stage II-IVB describe the use of MRD testing in routine clinical care. The cases were selected purposively, not consecutively, to span the contexts in which the results were interpreted: a positive result shortly before radiographic nodal recurrence (Case 1); a positive result during long-term adjuvant osimertinib preceding isolated mediastinal relapse (Case 2); a transient positive result with subsequent clearance and radiographic regression (Case 3); a positive result that prompted PET-CT revealing occult metastatic disease (Case 4); serially negative results concordant with sustained radiographic remission (Case 5); and a positive result that prompted comprehensive genomic profiling identifying an actionable KRAS G12C alteration (Case 6). Conclusions: Across Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, tissue-free MRD testing in NSCLC was used primarily during surveillance and often serially; first-test positivity was 15.7% (95% CI 10.9-22.2) overall, with wide and mutually overlapping confidence intervals across stages. The cases illustrate that MRD results may prompt diagnostic evaluation when interpreted alongside imaging and other clinical findings, but they are purposively selected, and treatment changes that followed a result are reported as description, not as evidence of benefit. No assay performance characteristic is estimated. These findings are hypothesis-generating; prospective, MRD-directed trials with standardized timepoints, thresholds, confirmatory strategies and pre-specified clinical actions are needed before MRD results can guide treatment.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lutetium-177 prostate-specific membrane antigen radioligand therapy ([177Lu]Lu-PSMA-RLT) is an effective treatment for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but no validated PSMA-PET/CT-based biomarker currently identifies patients at risk of early treatment failure. The aim of this study was to assess whether semi-quantitative PSMA-PET/CT parameters, in particular the fraction of PSMA-positive tumor volume with high uptake, are associated with early biochemical progression (EBP) and PSA50 response and secondarily with PSA-PFS and OS. Methods: Semiquantitative PSMA-PET parameters comprised reference lesion SUVmax (RL-SUVmax), SUVmean, total PSMA tumor volume (tPSMA-TV), tPSMA-TV above a fixed SUV threshold of 20 (tPSMA-TV20), the percentage of tPSMA-TV20 within tPSMA-TV (tPSMA-TV%), total lesion quotient (TLQ), TLQ20, and rTLQ%. The co-primary endpoints were EBP, defined as PSA progression according to the PCWG3 criteria within 4 months of the start of treatment, and PSA50 response, defined as a reduction in PSA of at least 50% compared with baseline. PSA-PFS (PCWG3-defined PSA progression or death from any cause) and OS were secondary endpoints. Results: 63 patients were retrospectively included (median follow-up, 20.9 months). In univariable analyses, higher baseline tPSMA-TV% was significantly associated with lower odds of EBP (OR per 10% increase, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.57-0.87; p = 0.001) and higher odds of PSA50 response (OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.07-1.61; p = 0.009). It was associated with longer PSA-PFS (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.67-0.84; p < 0.001) and longer OS (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.72-0.91; p < 0.001). Exploratory ROC analysis identified a tPSMA-TV% cut-off of 47.54% for EBP (AUC, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.57-0.86]; sensitivity, 0.61; specificity, 0.93), although this threshold requires external validation. In exploratory models including tPSMA-TV and SUVmean, tPSMA-TV% remained associated with PSA-PFS and OS but not with EBP or PSA50 response. Conclusions: Baseline tPSMA-TV% was associated with EBP, PSA50 response, PSA-PFS and OS in mCRPC patients undergoing [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-RLT, and these associations remained after adjustment for baseline PSA and metastatic presentation. tPSMA-TV% is a candidate prognostic imaging biomarker that requires external validation.

papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) are the most common malignant mesenchymal tumors that compose a heterogeneous group due to various molecular alterations. This study aimed to determine the molecular characteristics of patients with GIST treated between 2002 and 2017 and to follow their overall survival (OS) over 20 years. DNA was isolated from surgical biopsies of 490 patients with gut sarcomas and was analyzed using PCR and Sanger sequencing of hotspots of KIT, PDGFRA and BRAF genes. Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was used to determine SDHB expression. 417 GIST patients, including 13 children, were included; females predominated (male-to-female ratio 0.65), median age of 55.4 years old. KIT and PDGFRA mutations were found in 288 GISTs (69.1%) and 52 (12.5%), respectively. A total of 25 KIT and 3 novel PDGFRA mutations were revealed in 30 GISTs. KIT/PDGFRA mutations were not detected in 77 (18.5%) GISTs; among them were 2 NF1 GISTs, 10 with BRAF mutation, 14 with SDHB deficiency, and 3 "pediatric" GISTs. The overall survival (OS) of 280 GIST patients over more than 20 years. Genetic changes have a certain prognostic value in addition to such factors as tumor size, mitotic index, and location. The OS of GIST patients with KIT mutations was lower than that of patients with PDGFRA mutation, BRAF mutation, or SDHB deficiency, but the difference was non-significant. Our study highlights the heterogeneous nature and molecular features of GISTs in Russian population. The precise molecular characterization of the tumor should be considered an integral part of modern personalized GIST treatment.

papers.abstract: Background: Ovarian cancer (OC) poses an escalating global health burden, with marked disparities in incidence, mortality, and survivorship. Social, psychological, and structural determinants, including deprivation, stigma, and access to specialist care, may influence outcomes but are not well-represented in existing models of cancer care. We introduce the Tumour, Macroenvironment and Resource (TMR) framework, a novel conceptual model exploring interactions among tumour biology, social determinants, and healthcare resources in OC survivorship and care. Methods: Framework development occurred in three phases. First, a narrative review identified factors influencing OC outcomes across tumour, macroenvironmental, and healthcare resource domains. Second, multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) was used to structure these factors within a preliminary framework and assign indicative domain weightings. Third, two cross-sectional expert opinion surveys were conducted to refine and validate the concept of the framework. The final model was then evaluated in a retrospective pilot cohort to assess the feasibility of collecting predefined TMR variables from routinely available clinical data. Results: The review identified limited evidence addressing broader determinants of health beyond biological prognostic factors. Available studies suggested interactions between tumour characteristics, social determinants, and healthcare infrastructure that may influence outcomes. A preliminary model allocated 50% weighting to tumour factors and 50% to combined macroenvironmental and healthcare resource factors. Expert surveys (n = 20 and n = 44) achieved consensus and informed development of the final TMR framework. Application to a UK pilot cohort of patients with OC (n = 42) demonstrated the feasibility of collecting variables across all TMR domains and identified multiple adverse factors across tumour, macroenvironmental, and resource domains. Conclusions: The TMR framework provides an integrative, hypothesis-generating model for exploring disparities in OC survivorship and care. Further retrospective and prospective validation are required before clinical or prognostic applications can be considered.

papers.abstract: Ethnic inequalities in cancer incidence and outcomes are widespread, although the evidence available for people in the UK is more limited than in some other countries. This narrative review details the current evidence relating to ethnicity and differences in primary care cancer diagnosis in the UK and possible contributing factors. In general, cancer rates are higher for White individuals than for Asian or Black individuals in the UK, but for some cancer sites, the inverse is true. There are also differences in stage at diagnosis by ethnic group for some cancer sites. The routes through which cancer inequalities emerge are complex and difficult to attribute to a single patient characteristic. A variety of social, demographic, genetic and health service factors interact to influence outcomes. There is a wide research base demonstrating that Asian and Black individuals in the UK can experience a range of obstacles when interacting with health care services, including cancer investigations. Future research evidence and health service planning needs to include a diverse range of stakeholders in order to decrease cancer inequalities.

papers.abstract: Artificial spin ices have transcended their origins in frustrated rare-earth pyrochlores to become a versatile platform for engineering exotic states of matter. Across diverse implementations, from nanomagnets and superconducting vortices to colloids, quantum annealers, liquid crystals, and metamaterials, they are frequently described by the ice rule, often leading to degeneracy and constrained disorder by enforcing minimization of the local topological charge. Here, we report the realization of an "anti-spin ice" in which not only the ice rule does not hold, but its opposite is true as the system seeks to maximize, rather than minimize, spin ice charges. Using fast-rotating in-plane magnetic fields to generate isotropic attraction between colloidal particles, we invert the conventional paradigm of repulsive interactions in colloidal spin ices. Combining experiments and simulations across bipartite square and honeycomb lattices as well as non-bipartite pentaheptite geometries, we establish rules for order and disorder in the anti-spin ice. With the pentaheptite lattice, we demonstrate that the anti-spin ice system can also exhibit frustration, but of a different kind. This topological charge frustration arises from the lattice connectivity, where networks of unequal, odd-sided polygons suppress charge crystallization at high interaction strengths.

papers.abstract: Achieving precise integration of chiral microenvironments and catalytic metals in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a formidable challenge, often resulting in amorphous materials with poor stability and metal leaching. Here, we introduce a modular multivariate approach strategy coupled with post-synthetic metalation to engineer metal-chiral COFs (MCCOFs) with tunable crystallinity, porosity, and stereocontrol. Co-condensation of chiral Boc-protected diamines with variable achiral diamine ratios and tritopic aldehydes produced three crystalline frameworks (CCOFX-Boc, X = 0-2). Ruthenium metalation afforded CCOF2-Ru, which catalyzes asymmetric transfer hydrogenation of ketones with >99% yield, 97% ee, and a TOF of 1104 h-1. The catalyst exhibits broad substrate tolerance, including pharmacologically relevant chroman-4-ols, and maintains ≥95% ee over 5 gram-scale cycles with minimal Ru leaching (0.1 wt%). This approach upgrades unstable binary COFs into robust MCCOFs, enhancing activity, enantioselectivity, and durability via optimized pore architecture. It establishes a versatile platform for leaching-resistant chiral catalysts, advancing sustainable enantiopure pharmaceutical synthesis.

papers.abstract: Primary motor cortex (M1) plays a central role in voluntary movement, but how it integrates sensory-driven corrective instructions is unclear. We analyzed population activity recorded from M1 of male macaques during a sequential arm movement task with target updates requiring online adjustments to the motor plan. Using Latent Factor Analysis via Dynamical Systems (LFADS), we separated neural activity into two components: intrinsic dynamics and inferred external inputs. Inferred input timing was more strongly locked to target appearance than to movement onset, suggesting that variable reaction times reflect interactions between inputs and ongoing dynamics. Inferred inputs were tuned similarly for initial and corrective movements, suggesting shared input encoding across visually-instructed and corrective movements previously obscured by M1 dynamics. Because input inference can suffer from nonidentifiability, where different models fit data indistinguishably, we used ensembles of models with varied hyperparameters to diagnose when inputs are identifiable or nonidentifiable. In the monkey data, ensembles produced consistently similar results, suggesting that inputs could be meaningfully inferred and that their encoding was not simply a result of model bias. These results highlight the challenges of nonidentifiability and the potential of model ensembles to identify inputs in ongoing dynamics, at least in some cases.

papers.abstract: Diatom-bacteria interactions drive biogeochemical fluxes at the base of the marine food-web. Although bacteria are increasingly recognised as important drivers of algal mortality, the diversity of algicidal strategies remains understudied. Here we show that Alteromonas macleodii, a recurrent member of Thalassiosira rotula's microbiome, breaches the diatom's silica frustule, inducing >95% of cells to emerge from their shells within 72 h, exposing protoplasts to lysis and exploitation. Whilst protoplast formation was induced by diverse bacteria, A. macleodii uniquely caused population-wide collapse, used here to characterise this diatom stress response. Dual transcriptomics indicated the presence of a programmed necrosis-like cell death pathway in diatoms underpinning T. rotula's terminal morphological change, alongside upregulation of bacterial motility, chemotaxis and opportunistic metabolism. These findings reveal a potent algicidal strategy, recasting A. macleodii as an antagonist that exploits diatom mortality for its own benefit, removes the ballast provided by their frustules and thus reshapes oceanic carbon cycling.

papers.abstract: We theoretically demonstrate that transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) exhibit oscillatory and sign-reversing dynamic modulation in transmittance on the order of a few optical cycles under extreme electron temperatures, providing a possible explanation for TCO dynamics observed in earlier experiments. We present an inverse-designed multilayer cavity incorporating an ultrathin TCO layer, which supports an oscillatory optical response more pronounced than those previously observed experimentally in TCOs. This approach yields transmittance oscillations with a characteristic period of ~ 20 fs, which corresponds to approximately four optical cycles of the 1.431 μm probe beam. To achieve a similar oscillatory modulation in Δn, we incorporate a TCO electron-acceptor layer on top of the inverse-designed cavity, enabling thermionic carrier injection at the TCO junction. The resulting acceptor layer exhibits a striking Δn response as fast as 20 fs, corresponding to only three optical cycles of the 1.8-2.0 μm probe, and can be further tailored into the sub-optical-cycle regime. The findings could both clarify the previously unexplained transient dynamics in TCOs and, for the first time, demonstrate the critical role of electron temperatures in driving oscillatory dynamic responses.

papers.abstract: Isotonic (constant neutron number) systematics in the deformed rare-earth region have long suggested that nuclei with odd numbers of protons are more compact than their even-proton neighbors-except for Lu, whose recommended nuclear charge radius appeared anomalously large relative to Yb and Hf. We report a high-precision determination of the natural-abundance-averaged Lu-Yb charge-radius difference using extreme-ultraviolet spectroscopy of highly charged Na- and Mg-like ions, supported by high-accuracy relativistic atomic-structure calculations-a recently introduced method with the unique ability to measure inter-element charge-radius differences. Combined with muonic-atom and optical isotope-shift data, our results reestablish a pronounced odd-even staggering along the isotonic chain with neutron number N = 94. Nuclear density functional theory calculations, including quantified uncertainties, fail to reproduce the large stagger, while successfully reproducing the charge-radii staggering along isotopic chains and in semi-magic nuclei. In this work, we resolve the Lu inversion anomaly and provide new constraints for experimental and theoretical studies of nuclear size.

papers.abstract: Exciton transport is fundamental for understanding transport phenomena in bosonic systems and for exploring excitation energy transfer in materials. Spatially indirect excitons (IXs) have long lifetimes allowing them to form quantum bosonic states and travel long distances. Van der Waals heterostructures form a new materials platform for exploring IX transport. Disordered in-plane potentials suppress IX transport due to IX localization and scattering. In this work, we found the efficient IX transport kinetics characterized by anomalously high IX mobility. The efficient IX transport kinetics is observed in the presence of substantial in-plane disorder. The anomalously high IX mobility, its disappearance with increasing temperature, and its non-monotonic dependence on density are qualitatively consistent with theoretical predictions of IX superfluidity.

papers.abstract: The transmembrane export apparatus is a conserved core of bacterial type III secretion systems shared by flagella and injectisomes. Powered by the proton-motive force (PMF), this machinery translocates protein substrates across the cytoplasmic membrane to support bacterial motility and virulence. However, how the export apparatus assembles and functions within native membranes remains poorly understood. Here, using in situ single-particle cryo-electron microscopy and cryo-electron tomography, we resolve high-resolution structures of the flagellar export apparatus within intact cells of the Lyme disease spirochete Borrelia burgdorferi. Structural and genetic analyses suggest that coordinated assembly of the export apparatus and MS-ring drives extensive deformation of the cytoplasmic membrane, generating a funnel-shaped conduit for substrate translocation. The FlhA nonamer and FliPQR-FlhB export gate lack direct transmembrane contacts and are separated by a thin, bilayer-like density, revealing a lipid-mediated interface. The conserved FlhB hinge helix extends into the FlhA tunnel and may couple PMF-driven energy transduction to substrate translocation. We further identify a conserved hydrophilic pathway within FlhA and show that key acidic residues lining this pathway are essential for export activity. Together, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for export apparatus assembly and energy transduction, providing broader insights into type III secretion.

papers.abstract: Active systems across scales, ranging from molecular machines to human crowds, are usually modeled as assemblies of self-propelled particles driven by internally generated forces. However, these models often assume memoryless dynamics. Here, guided by the example of living cells, which have recently been shown to display multi-timescale memory effects, we introduce a minimal theoretical framework that incorporates internal state dynamics and environmental sensing into overdamped active particle models of cell migration. We show that when the self-propulsion depends on internal variables with their own complex dynamics-modulated by local environmental cues- environmental memory spontaneously emerges and gives rise to new classes of behaviours. These include memory-induced responses, adaptable localization in complex landscapes, suppression of motility-induced phase separation, and enhanced jamming transitions. Our results demonstrate how minimal information processing capabilities, intrinsic to nonequilibrium agents with internal states like living cells, can profoundly influence both individual and collective behaviours. This framework bridges cell-scale activity and large-scale intelligent motion in cell assemblies, and opens the way to the quantitative analysis and design of systems ranging from synthetic colloids to biological collectives and robotic swarms.

papers.abstract: Survival and transmission of the human pathogen Trypanosoma cruzi depend on dynamic remodeling of its membrane proteome, yet the post-translational networks governing this plasticity remain obscure. Using metabolic labeling and quantitative mass spectrometry, we present a comprehensive map of the T. cruzi S-palmitoylome: a high-confidence atlas of 254 proteins enriched for signaling factors, cytoskeletal regulators, and membrane transporters. Functional screening with our aptazyme-based SHARK knockdown system identifies ABCA10, an uncharacterized ABC transporter central to heme homeostasis. Depletion of ABCA10 triggers a compensatory surge in cytostome-mediated endocytosis, rendering this normally dispensable process conditionally essential. ABCA10 expression is itself heme-regulated and upon heme starvation it redistributes from the flagellar pocket to pre-lysosomal reservosomes. We further show that endocytosis is directly tuned by extracellular heme, placing the entire uptake apparatus, not only ABCA10, under heme-responsive control. Together, these findings reveal a redundant heme-scavenging strategy and expose a druggable vulnerability in a neglected pathogen.

papers.abstract: Leiomodin 1 (LMOD1) was previously reported to be associated with longer survival in leiomyosarcoma (LMS) in analysis combining uterine and non-uterine tumors. The objective of the present study was to analyze the expression and prognostic role of LMOD1 in a large series of exclusively uterine LMS (uLMS). LMOD1 protein expression by immunohistochemistry was analyzed in tissue microarrays (TMAs) from 244 uLMS and whole sections from 203 uLMS, of which 134 were included in both series. Expression was assessed for association with clinicopathologic parameters and disease-specific survival (DSS). TMAs were informative in 221/244 (91%) tumors, of which 100 (45%) expressed LMOD1. No significant association with DSS was observed for 156 patients with clinical data. In the series stained using whole sections, LMOD1 was expressed in 142/203 (70%) tumors, and higher expression was associated with significantly longer survival (203 patients with survival data; p=0.007). Other parameters related to survival in the latter series were FIGO stage (p<0.001), tumor diameter (p<0.001), mitotic count (p<0.001), the degree of atypia (p=0.006) and lymphovascular invasion (LVSI; p=0.006). In Cox multivariate analysis, FIGO stage (p<0.001), mitotic count (p<0.001), tumor diameter (p=0.001) and LMOD1 expression (p=0.003) were independent prognosticators. LMOD1 expression in whole sections is a new candidate marker of longer survival in uLMS. This study additionally highlights the limitations associated with use of TMA sections compared to whole sections in biomarker studies.

papers.abstract: Greater adiposity is associated with higher postmenopausal but lower premenopausal breast cancer risk; whether its metabolic consequences - insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and atherogenic lipoproteins - follow the same pattern is unresolved. Apolipoproteins, which track with adiposity, have not to our knowledge been evaluated prospectively for premenopausal breast cancer risk in East Asia. We examined these markers in relation to incident breast cancer in Korean women. We followed 99,648 Korean women (91.3% premenopausal) without prior breast cancer attending health screening during 2011-2024. Prespecified exposures were metabolic syndrome component count, the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), a fatty-liver proxy, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), and the apolipoprotein B (ApoB) to apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) ratio. Incident breast cancer was ascertained by registry linkage (ICD-10 C50 plus D05). Age-stratified Cox models used sequential adjustment; the primary model included reproductive, anthropometric, and lifestyle covariates. Over a median 7.75 years of follow-up, 1094 incident breast cancers occurred (28.1% in situ). In the primary model, metabolic syndrome component count (hazard ratio 1.05 per component, 95% CI 0.97-1.14), HOMA-IR (1.01 per log unit, 0.91-1.12), and hs-CRP (0.98 per log unit, 0.90-1.06) were not associated with breast cancer risk; the fatty-liver estimate was uninformative (38 exposed cases). The ApoB/ApoA1 ratio (0.94 per 1 SD, 0.88-1.00) and ApoB (0.94, 0.88-1.00) were inversely but not significantly associated, both attenuating to the null in a 3-year landmark analysis (0.99, 0.92-1.07). ApoB and LDL cholesterol were near-collinear (r = 0.944), precluding specificity analyses. Metabolic and apolipoprotein markers were not associated with breast cancer risk in this predominantly premenopausal Korean cohort. These sequelae therefore do not appear to share the inverse association adiposity shows before menopause. These are, to our knowledge, the first prospective apolipoprotein data on premenopausal breast cancer risk in East Asian women.

papers.abstract: Australia prohibited commercial solariums in 2015 to reduce exposure to artificial ultraviolet (UV) radiation, an established and preventable cause of melanoma. However, evidence of population-level effects on melanoma incidence, mortality, and clinical severity remains limited. To evaluate whether the commercial solarium ban was associated with immediate and longer-term changes in melanoma incidence, mortality, and clinical severity nationally and across states and demographic, geographic, and tumour-thickness subgroups. We conducted a quasi-experimental regression discontinuity study using three population-based datasets from the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare. Analyses examined national melanoma incidence (1982-2021), mortality (1971-2021), state-specific trends across six states accounting for Western Australia's 2016 implementation, and clinical severity using Breslow thickness and other histopathological indicators. Parametric ordinary least squares models with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors were complemented by non-parametric local polynomial analyses. Robustness was assessed using alternative bandwidths, kernel specifications, and placebo cutoffs. At the national level, the commercial solarium ban was associated with an estimated immediate reduction of 3.86 melanoma cases per 100,000 population and 2.28 melanoma deaths per 100,000 population. However, neither reduction was statistically significant (p = 0.493 and p = 0.171, respectively). Following the ban, the annual incidence trend decreased by 2.00 cases per 100,000 among males (p 2-4 mm), while melanomas thicker > 4 mm exhibited an immediate reduction following the ban. Queensland and Western Australia experienced declining incidence trends, with a corresponding decline in mortality trends in Western Australia. The ban was not associated with an abrupt nationwide reduction in melanoma incidence or mortality but coincided with improvements in selected demographic, geographic, and tumour-thickness groups. These heterogeneous patterns suggest a potential gradual policy effect rather than an immediate population-wide decline.

papers.abstract: Accelerated biological aging has been reported in certain racial/ethnic groups, raising concerns about widening outcome disparities with age. This phenomenon has not been adequately explored in cancer outcomes. National Cancer Database (2010-2021) was used to analyze outcomes in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients by race/ethnicity and age at diagnosis: < 65, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, and ≥ 80 years. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and 90-day postoperative mortality (PM), analyzed with multivariable regression. In this large national cohort study of 585,729 patients, non-Hispanic Black (nHB) patients had worse OS across all age groups, with the largest disparity in the < 65 group (median OS: 64.1 in nHB vs. 127.0 months in non-Hispanic White (nHW); HR 1.28, 95% CI 1.26-1.30) and smaller disparity in ≥ 80 group (median OS: 19.2 in nHB vs. 26.5 months in nHW; HR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09). The 90-day PM in nHB patients was higher than nHW, particularly in the < 65 (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.15-1.31) group. In contrast to non-oncological literature, we did not observe widening racial/ethnic disparities with age. Largest disparities were found in younger age groups suggesting differences in tumor biology may play a more important factor for cancer outcomes.
