papers.abstract: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) is an established therapeutic target in ovarian cancer, but information on its expression distribution, staining heterogeneity, and molecular context in Chinese patients remains limited. We evaluated these features in ovarian high grade serous carcinoma (HGSC). This retrospective multicenter study included 1002 patients with resected HGSC from 14 Chinese hospitals. FRα expression was assessed using the VENTANA FOLR1 (FOLR1-2.1) RxDx Assay based on the percentage of viable tumor cells with moderate or strong (2+/3+) membranous staining. Intensity specific percentages were available for 992 tumors. Associations with clinicopathologic features and BRCA1/2, HRD, TMB, MSI, MMR, HER2, and PD-L1 were exploratory. Temporal concordance was evaluated in 53 paired primary and recurrent tumors. High FRα expression, defined as 2+/3+ staining in ≥75% of viable tumor cells, was observed in 435 of 1002 tumors (43.41%). Among 992 tumors with intensity data, 972 (98.0%) contained at least two staining categories, and 924 (93.1%) contained both negative or weak and moderate or strong tumor cell populations. No significant associations were detected with age, FIGO stage, tumor size, or the biomarkers evaluated, although analyses were limited and underpowered. Paired tumors showed 71.7% categorical agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.44) and moderate correlation of FRα percentages (Spearman ρ = 0.59). FRα expression showed substantial variation between tumors and frequent intensity admixture within specimens. Biomarker associations remain inconclusive because of limited testing. Moderate primary and recurrent concordance supports archival testing, while discordance suggests repeat testing at recurrence may be appropriate in selected patients.

papers.abstract: Abstract Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

papers.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV) causes severe hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and is uniquely capable of person-to-person transmission, with no licenced vaccines or therapeutics available. A Phase 1 trial (NCT03682107) demonstrated that an ANDV DNA vaccine targeting Gn/Gc envelope proteins elicits neutralising antibodies in humans. We evaluated whether these human antibodies protect against lethal disease in an animal model. Day 197 sera from vaccinated human subjects were pooled, purified, and passively transferred to female Syrian hamsters one day prior to lethal ANDV challenge across two independent experiments. Controls included normal human IgG, PBS (negative controls), and SAB-400 (positive control). Neutralising antibody levels were quantified using pseudovirion neutralisation assays (PsVNA) and plaque reduction neutralisation tests (PRNT) to determine exploratory cutoff titres predicting survival. Human antibodies from DNA-vaccinated subjects-unlike normal IgG-conferred significant protection against lethal ANDV challenge in both experiments. The exploratory cutoff titres predicting protection were determined to be 31-184 for PsVNA50 and 20-80 for PRNT50, depending on the analysis population and model parameters. Vaccine-induced human antibodies are sufficient to protect against lethal ANDV infection in an established animal model. If confirmed, these results indicate that neutralising antibody titres could serve as a surrogate endpoint and correlate of protection for future hantavirus Gn/Gc-targeted vaccines. papers.abstract: Bile acids represent one of nature's most chemically diverse and therapeutically important metabolite families. However, the human bile acid metabolome remains largely uncharted, with analytical limitations obscuring potentially thousands of biologically active species present in cells and biofluids. Here, we present MetLLM, a transformer-based language model that learns bile acid modification patterns to prioritize candidate bile acid analogs, and MetSpace, an in silico bile acid chemical landscape containing 3,900 prioritized candidates. Liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry analysis of human feces confirmed multiple newly detected and structurally novel bile acids, including MS2141 and MS1281. In vitro functional validation showed that MS2141 modulates M2 receptor-associated Gi/o signaling and alters electrophysiological parameters in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. This work expands the searchable bile acid metabolome and provides a computational framework for systematic metabolite discovery.

papers.abstract: Rare variants are highly abundant, yet their genome-wide contributions to agronomic traits remain elusive in plants. Here, we performed deep whole-genome sequencing of 3,367 diverse elite maize inbred lines, uncovering 75.3 million variants, of which 79.2% were rare. Overall, we identified 411 independent association signals for 10 agronomic traits, including 359 attributable to globally rare variants, with rare variants showing effect sizes approximately 2.4 times those of common variants. Frequency-stratified genome-based restricted maximum likelihood (GREML) analyses indicated that rare variants captured a substantial proportion of phenotypic variance for traits under strong adaptive selection, consistent with the allele frequencies of trait-associated variants shifting from common in tropical to rare in temperate maize. Complementing conventional variant-level genome-wide association studies (GWAS), gene-based tests identified an additional 94 candidate gene-trait associations. Our study highlights rare variants as important components of the genetic architecture of complex agronomic traits in maize and provides much-needed resources for future functional studies and breeding.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of several malignancies; however, their efficacy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) remains limited. The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in ovarian cancer constitutes a major barrier to effective antitumor immunity, prompting the development of various strategies to enhance responsiveness to ICIs. This narrative review examines current therapeutic approaches targeting the TME to overcome resistance to ICIs in PROC, with a focus on angiogenesis, innate immunity, and adaptive immune pathways. Despite a strong biological rationale, most chemotherapy-free ICI-based combinations targeting specific immune or stromal components have shown limited and inconsistent clinical benefit. The most notable clinical activity has been observed when ICIs are combined with chemotherapy, particularly in regimens that include anti-angiogenic agents. Recent positive results from a single phase 3 trial evaluating pembrolizumab in combination with weekly paclitaxel, with or without bevacizumab, mark a notable deviation from the predominantly negative outcomes of earlier studies. Nevertheless, it remains uncertain whether this result represents a true paradigm shift or a context-specific effect. Currently, no validated predictive biomarkers exist to reliably identify patients most likely to benefit from ICI-based strategies. The discrepancy between the isolated success of chemo-immunotherapy combinations and the failure of most previous trials highlights the need for further investigation into TME biology. A more comprehensive understanding of TME dynamics and the development of biomarker-driven patient selection strategies will be essential to define the role of ICIs in this challenging clinical context.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. PPP1R1B was significantly upregulated in non-responders and correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. PPP1R1B-mediated inhibition of IFN-β signaling reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and impaired antitumor immunity, ultimately conferring resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background SpliceAI is a deep learning algorithm that predicts whether genetic variants are likely to affect splicing. Precomputed SpliceAI predictions for all theoretical SNVs and small indels were released in 2019, and are used by variant annotation tools such as VEP and dbNSFP to batch annotate large numbers of variants quickly. While the use of precomputed scores vastly reduces the computational cost of retrieving SpliceAI predictions, several limitations to their utility have emerged, for which the impact on the prioritisation of likely splice-altering variants in cohort studies has not been established. Methods We identify transcript annotation and genome version inconsistencies impacting the precomputed SpliceAI scores by comparing the original gene annotation file with MANE v1.0 Select transcripts. To quantify the impact that these factors may have in variant prioritisation pipelines for diagnostic purposes, we re-analysed variants in 660 genes linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), identified in 7,221 participants with NDD from the Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project (100kGP). Results We find outdated gene annotations and genome version inconsistencies impact 8.34% of theoretical SNVs included in the SpliceAI precomputed scores, and affect the accuracy of SpliceAI predictions in 34.98% of disease-associated panelApp green genes. In 7,221 Genomics England participants, re-running SpliceAI with updated annotations and parameters results in an increase of 18.2% predicted splice-altering variants compared with variants identified using precomputed scores alone. These variants constitute a diagnostic increase of 11.7% versus the precomputed scores, assessed retrospectively using confirmed diagnoses in 100kGP. To mitigate issues with the precomputed scores we provide ‘SpliceAI-splint’- a command-line tool to allow users to identify variants within a VCF file whose potential splice-altering effects would be missed by the precomputed scores. Conclusions: Although the precomputed scores continue to represent a useful resource in the annotation of variants in cohorts with genetic disorders, we find key limitations that can lead to their missing clinically relevant splice-altering variants, and provide a command-line tool to mitigate these issues.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Ciprofloxacin resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae is common or emerging in many geographies, and knowledge of local resistance rates is important for empirical therapy. While K. pneumoniae ciprofloxacin resistance determinants are known, there is a lack of systematic data on the effect of these determinants, alone and in combination, and there are no publicly accessible tools for predicting ciprofloxacin resistance from whole genome sequence data. Methods The KlebNET-GSP AMR Genotype-Phenotype Group aggregated a matched genotype-phenotype dataset of n = 12,167 K. pneumoniae species complex ( Kp SC) isolates from 27 countries between 2001 and 2021. We developed a rule-based classifier to predict ciprofloxacin resistance by categorizing the number of mutations in the quinolone resistance determining regions of gyrA and parC and the number of plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes, including the presence/absence of aac(6 ' )-Ib-cr (which can acetylate ciprofloxacin). Predictive performance was assessed using the discovery dataset, with the reassessment of discrepant and concordant isolates; and validated using externally contributed datasets ( n = 7,030 Kp SC isolates). Results The rule-based classifier predicted R vs S/I with categorical agreement, sensitivity, and specificity > 96%, and major/very major error rates < 4%. Performance was similar across diverse Kp SC sources (human, animal, other), species, and intra-species lineages. External validation of the classifier yielded overall 90.18% categorical agreement [95% confidence interval (CI), 89.49–90.88%], 8.74% major errors [95% CI, 7.41–10.06%], 4.19% very major errors [95% CI, 3.60–4.77%], and 10.14% minor errors [95% CI, 9.44–10.85%]. We implemented the classifier in Kleborate, a command-line tool that is integrated into the Pathogenwatch web platform. Using this to assess the global distribution of ciprofloxacin resistance determinants in Kp SC genomes available in Pathogenwatch ( n = 31,319, from 109 countries between years 2000–2023), we observed a significant positive association between national quinolone consumption rates and predicted ciprofloxacin resistance (R 2 = 0.20, p = 0.004). Conclusion Ciprofloxacin resistance phenotypes can be reasonably predicted from genotype, which is sufficient for informing surveillance. However, unexplained resistance remains and accuracy is insufficient for clinical applications. We demonstrate the value of aggregating genotype-phenotype data to explore resistance mechanisms and develop predictors, but highlight complexities in combining phenotype data from different assays and standards.

papers.abstract: Reactivation of human herpesviruses (HHVs), particularly EBV, is associated with more severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of Long COVID (LC). Reactivation of HHVs has been previously implicated in hormonal dysregulation, which has also been observed in LC, suggesting a potential link. This study aims to examine the relationship between LC symptoms and salivary HHV DNA, cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol levels. Our cross-sectional, case-control study enrolled 45 participants with LC, and 45 age-sex-matched controls. Surveys and validated health questionnaires were used to collect demographics, medical history, and symptom profiles. Saliva was self-collected at waking, 15, 30, and 45 min, and 8 and 16 h after waking, across two consecutive days. Salivary cortisol, testosterone and oestradiol were measured, and extracted nucleic acid was tested for EBV, HSV 1/2, HCMV and HHV-6 A/B using multiplex qPCR, and for SARS-CoV-2 and RNaseP using RT-qPCR. Detection of salivary EBV and HHV-6 DNA copies was highest early in the morning. There were no significant differences in salivary cortisol, testosterone, or oestradiol, or in EBV or HHV-6 DNA between the LC and control groups. However, salivary HHV-6 DNA levels were positively associated with a greater aggregated LC propensity score (r = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.02-0.44, p = 0.015, adj. p = 0.030), as well as anxiety (β = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.02-1.36, p = 0.045) and depression (β = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.05-0.42, p = 0.013) scores. The observed correlation between salivary HHV-6 DNA and symptom severity suggests HHV-6 may contribute to post-acute disease, though mechanisms remain unclear. While we did not identify a relationship between salivary EBV DNA and LC, EBV may still play a role at earlier time points in the disease course, or in compartments not sampled in this study. These findings highlight the potential importance of HHV-6 in LC pathophysiology and underscore the need for longitudinal, multi-compartment studies of herpesvirus reactivation in LC. National Institutes for Health (NIH) funding sources supported AT, SB and CM.

papers.abstract: Disease-associated loci identified by genome-wide association studies (GWASs) may induce effects by altering transcription factor (TF) binding. However, due to the scarcity of population-level TF-binding experiments, identifying these disrupted TFs remains challenging. To address this, we present the TFXcan framework, which correlates genetically predicted TF binding with phenotypes to nominate TF-tissue pairs that may regulate complex traits. Within this framework, we introduce Enpact, a deep learning-based approach that integrates Enformer and IMPACT to infer personalized TF-binding events. Leveraging Enpact, we correlate predicted binding profiles for 700 TF-tissue pairs with prostate cancer risk, identifying multiple implicated TFs at risk loci. Matrix decomposition further reveals clusters of TF-tissue pairs, termed "programs," acting as candidate drivers of disease risk. TFXcan represents the first method capable of predicting TF binding from genotype data at scale, enabling systematic identification of TFs and regulatory programs underlying complex traits.

papers.abstract: The BCMA×CD3 bispecific T cell engager (TCE) transforms targeted immunotherapy but remains constrained by ex vivo manufacturing and systemic delivery, limiting its application in autoimmune disorders. Here, we use a T cell-targeted integration-deficient lentiviral vector (T-IDLE) to program endogenous T cells to secrete BCMA×CD3 TCEs directly in vivo. In a murine model of Sjögren's syndrome-associated dry eye, a single intravenous administration of T-IDLESTCE achieves deep but time-limited depletion of plasmablasts and plasma cells, reverses lacrimal gland inflammation, and restores tear production without detectable off-target transduction. Longitudinal studies in cynomolgus monkeys demonstrate plasma cell clearance and a favorable safety profile. Mechanistic analyses show that secreted TCEs redirect nearby non-activated T cells against BCMA-expressing targets in vitro and that the treatment attenuates T helper 1 (Th1)/Th17-mediated inflammation while eliciting controlled cytokine responses in vivo. This approach avoids individualized ex vivo T cell manufacturing and represents a scalable immunotherapy strategy for autoantibody-mediated diseases.

papers.abstract: The tumor-associated microenvironment, shaped by dynamic crosstalk between tumor cells and peritumoral adipose tissue (PAT), has attracted growing attention in recent years. Beyond serving as a passive energy reservoir, PAT actively contributes to tumor progression through metabolic reprogramming, modulation of immune cell function, and remodeling of the stromal vascular fraction. Conversely, tumors induce profound structural and functional reorganization in PAT, including fibrosis, browning, and systemic effects such as cachexia, which further enhances tumor progression. Together, these changes reinforce a tumor-supportive microenvironment. Collectively, these reciprocal interactions underscore the pivotal role of adipose tissue in shaping tumor behavior. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the multifaceted roles of PAT in tumor development, elucidates the mechanisms underlying the bidirectional tumor-adipose interaction, and discusses emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the adipose-tumor axis as a promising avenue for cancer treatment.

papers.abstract: Postnatal depression (PND) is associated with offspring neurodevelopmental impairments, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify an intergenerational pathway whereby maternal psychological state is encoded in breastmilk microRNAs (miRNAs) and transmitted to offspring via small extracellular vesicles (sEVs). Using cross-fostering models, we show that maternal depression disrupts newborn neuron maturation in the offspring hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG), causing cognitive deficits and depressive-like behaviors. Gastric administration of PND-derived breastmilk sEVs to healthy pups recapitulates these phenotypes. Mechanistically, PND-induced miRNAs are packaged into breastmilk sEVs and delivered to the offspring brain, where they suppress mGluR8 in supramammillary nucleus (SuM) neurons projecting to DG. This presynaptic mGluR8 deficiency drives a "high-frequency, low-amplitude" neuronal activation pattern. Inhibiting mammary sEV secretion or sequestering these miRNAs in offspring SuM neurons rescues the deficits. Our findings define a mechanism underlying PND-related offspring neurodevelopmental impairments and suggest a therapeutic target for interrupting the intergenerational transmission of maternal mental disorders.

papers.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is associated with chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), yet the incidence, severity, and optimal antiemetic prophylaxis remain uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify T-DXd-related nausea and vomiting and evaluate the effectiveness of triplet vs doublet prophylaxis. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched Ovid MEDLINE® ALL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library (1946 to June 2025) for studies reporting nausea and vomiting outcomes with T-DXd. The primary endpoint was pooled incidence of nausea and vomiting. Secondary endpoints included relative risk compared with standard therapies and comparative effectiveness of triplet vs doublet antiemetic prophylaxis. Thirty-two studies including 5365 patients (4224 T-DXd recipients) met inclusion. At the 5.4 mg/kg dose, pooled incidence was 65% for any-grade nausea and 31% for any-grade vomiting, with ≥ grade 3 events ≤4%. Incidence rates were similar at 6.4 mg/kg, with no significant dose-dependent increase in gastrointestinal toxicity (RR 0.96; 95% CI 0.83-1.11). Across five randomized trials, T-DXd significantly increased the risk of any-grade nausea 70.8% vs 28.4% (RR 2.29; 95% CI 1.74-3.02) and vomiting (RR 3.49; 95% CI 2.78-4.38) compared with standard therapies, while high-grade events remained uncommon (≤4%). Triplet antiemetic prophylaxis significantly improved delayed-phase nausea control (RR 1.27; 95% CI 1.03-1.58). Nausea and vomiting, particularly delayed nausea, are common with T-DXd, representing a major unmet supportive-care need. Triplet antiemetic prophylaxis improves delayed nausea control and should be considered. Future prospective studies incorporating patient-reported outcomes are needed to optimize prophylactic strategies. None.

papers.abstract: CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore are prognostic scores estimating the risk of recurrence after neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, but can they predict the long-term outcomes in a clinical trial? In this study, we assessed their surrogacy values at patient level and trial level for long-term outcomes, using data from 8,359 patients across nine neoadjuvant randomized trials conducted by the German Breast Group (GBG) and AGO-B study group. We found that at the patient level, both scores were significantly associated with outcomes, but at the trial level, the associations with distant disease-free survival (DDFS), invasive disease-free survival (iDFS), and overall survival (OS) were weak for both scores (R2 range = 0.03 to 0.24, with wide confidence intervals). Thus, our findings suggest that CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore are not reliable surrogate endpoints for predicting long-term treatment benefit in neoadjuvant trials but remain valuable for estimating individual patients' residual risk after neoadjuvant treatments and guiding subsequent treatment decisions for early breast cancer patients.

papers.abstract: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls. In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants. Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred. The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings. The Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

papers.abstract: Non-pharmacological techniques have recently been developed to decrease preoperative anxiety, and music or video may be combined, as in children. This study aims to compare two additional preoperative strategies in adult outpatients. This before-after trial was approved by the ethics committee and included adults undergoing ambulatory procedures under general anaesthesia. It compared usual care before surgery and another period with a video of the expected local journey combined with a relaxing music session. After consent, the level of anxiety was measured via the APAIS score, a repeated visual analogue scale for anxiety, and investigators collected preoperative fears. The main objective was to reduce the number of patients with significant preoperative anxiety. Secondary outcomes compared anxiety during the journey, pain, and quality of recovery after surgery. A P-value < 0.05 was considered significant. 99 patients were included in each period, and 194 completed the study. The intervention group showed a significant reduction in the rate of patients with significant anxiety at admission in the operating room: 23/95 (24.2%, 95%CI [16.7-33.7]) vs. 43/99 (43.4%, 95%CI [34.1-53.3]) with P = 0.005. Secondary outcomes showed no difference in anxiety after surgery, neither in length of stay nor incidence of PONV. The postoperative level of pain was also statistically reduced (P = 0.033). The study suggests that a combined video and music strategy decreases the rate of significant anxiety in patients undergoing outpatient procedures. This low-cost strategy showed a high level of satisfaction and should be encouraged in adults. Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT06461052.

papers.abstract: CD30+ T cell lymphoproliferative disorders (CD30+ T LPD) with cutaneous involvement comprise a diverse group of neoplasms with variable clinical outcomes. The molecular mechanisms underlying the prognostic differences in these diseases are poorly understood. In this multi-institutional retrospective study, 79 patients with CD30+ T LPD were evaluated. DNA and RNA sequencing were performed on skin biopsy samples to characterise molecular features. Patients were assigned to low- and high-risk groups based on treatment recommendations in clinical records. Pathogenic pathways, immune microenvironments, transcriptomic profiles, driver mutations, and mutation signatures were compared between the risk groups. Across risk groups, there was high mutational recurrence in genes involved in epigenetic regulation and intracellular signalling pathways. Mutational signature analysis revealed a shared prevalence of 5-methylcytosine deamination, UV exposure, defective mismatch repair, and POLE-associated proofreading deficiency. In contrast, gene set enrichment analysis showed that the high-risk group was enriched in pathways governing cell cycle progression, DNA damage response, and immune activation compared to the low-risk group. Furthermore, immune microenvironment deconvolution showed a higher abundance of resting dendritic cells in the low-risk group. Finally, high-risk patients exhibited significant overexpression of clinically relevant proteins, highlighting potential alternative treatment approaches for this population. Mutation analyses suggest diverse pathogenesis in these diseases. The high-risk and low-risk groups diverge in gene expression profiles and immune microenvironment, suggesting that these biological differences hold prognostic significance. Molecularly informed therapeutic strategies should be investigated prospectively through clinical trials. This work was supported by developmental funds of the Duke Cancer Institute as part of the P30 Cancer Center Support Grant. Data generation was supported in an unrestricted fashion by the NIH, Data Driven Bioscience, Amazon and Google. SSD was supported by the Wellcome Trust Foundation and the NIH.

papers.abstract: Due to limited resources, identifying high-risk surgical patients who derive clinical benefit from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission is essential. Our primary aim was to characterize resource allocation and evaluate the true clinical benefit of ICU admissions using modified Wang criteria. Secondary aim is to identify independent risk factors for ICU admission; validate clinical scoring systems; and compare inter-group outcomes, including Clavien-Dindo complication rates, lengths of stay, and mortality. This multicenter, prospective, observational study was conducted across 75 ICUs. Adult inpatient surgery cases were categorized into four groups: planned admission (PAG), unplanned admission (UPAG), planned but not admitted (PBNAG), and emergent admission (EAG). Data included preoperative/intraoperative/postoperative(ICU) variables, modified Wang criteria, and mortality rates (ICU, hospital, 30/90-day). Of 55,963 preoperatively evaluated patients, 2764 (4.9%) were planned for ICU admission; 804/2764 patients could not be admitted because of limited ICU beds, remaining of 1960 patients with a planned ICU admission, 411/1960 did not require postoperative ICU care forming the PBNAG (14.8% of 2764). Overall, 1980 patients (3.09% of all cases) were admitted to the ICU (78.2% PAG, 12.5% EAG, 9.1% UPAG). POSSUM scores effectively differentiated PBNAG (lower) and EAG (higher) from PAG. ICU benefit indicators (e.g., vasopressor need, prolonged ventilation >12 h, arrest events) were significantly higher in UPAG and EAG versus PAG (p 2 (OR 2.7) independently increased UPAG risk, whereas minimally invasive surgery and regional anesthesia reduced ICU admissions. Overall ICU and 90-day mortality rates were 5.9% and 7.5%, respectively, peaking in the EAG group (18.1% and 18.9%). Integrating modified Wang criteria, POSSUM scores, intraoperative complications, emergency status, and ASA class >2 is effective in predicting the necessity of ICU admission.

papers.abstract: Spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) guide extubation decisions in intensive care unit (ICU), predicting the respiratory effort required by the patient after extubation. Different SBTs exist and should be adapted to critical illness. Viral pneumonias such as COVID-19 combine lung injury, sepsis-induced systemic inflammation, and encephalopathy, making classification challenging. The objective was to assess which SBT could be used to reproduce postextubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients. In this multicenter randomized crossover study, COVID-19-related ARDS patients mechanically ventilated at least 24 hours and ready for extubation underwent 3 different 15-minute SBT at random order: pressure support ventilation of 7-cmH2O with positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 0-cmH2O (PSV7PEEP0), PSV 0-cmH2O with PEEP 0-cmH2O (PSV0PEEP0) and T-piece trial. At baseline, end of each SBT, and 20 minutes after extubation, surrogates of respiratory effort were measured: esophageal pressure-time-product (PTPes), PTPes per minute (PTPes.min), swing esophageal pressure (SwingPes), and SwingPes per minute (SwingPes.min). Sixty measurements of respiratory effort from 12 patients were analyzed. Median PTPes.min increased from 193.8 [170.8-227.2] cmH2O.s/min at baseline to 236.6 [192.1-313.6] after extubation, with no significant differences between SBTs and postextubation. SwingPes and SwingPes.min were lower during PSV7-PEEP0 than after extubation, with median paired differences of 4.7 (95% CI 0.6-9.8) and 115.3 (95% CI 4.8-297.8), but these differences did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. No SBT modality differed significantly from post-extubation respiratory effort, suggesting that none could be excluded in COVID-19-related ARDS patients.

papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is an important postoperative neurocognitive complication, and cumulative anticholinergic drug burden (ADB) may increase its risk by impairing central cholinergic neurotransmission. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to clarify the overall association between ADB scores and POD risk in adult surgical patients. We searched major databases and trial registries through February 2026 for studies that assessed ADB using validated scales and reported POD outcomes in adult surgical patients. Random-effects models pooled SMDs and ORs. Prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses explored heterogeneity and robustness. Risk of bias was assessed using NOS, and evidence certainty was rated using GRADE. Ten reports from nine independent cohorts comprising 10,457 participants were included. Patients with POD had higher ADB scores than those without POD (SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.20-0.43). Each one-point increase in continuous ADB was associated with 22% higher odds of POD (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.09-1.37). Both low-to-moderate and high burden were associated with increased POD risk. In scale-specific analyses, the association was significant for ACB. The association was attenuated in studies that excluded patients with cognitive impairment. Methodological quality ranged from moderate to high, and certainty of evidence was low. Higher ADB is significantly associated with higher odds of POD, with a graded increase in risk across burden levels. Baseline cognitive impairment appears to amplify this association. These findings support preoperative ADB assessment and medication optimization in vulnerable surgical patients, while highlighting the need for prospective head-to-head comparisons of anticholinergic burden scales. PROSPERO (CRD420261294941).

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by diffuse infiltration into the surrounding brain, limiting complete surgical resection, the strongest determinant of patient survival. The mechanisms driving this invasive growth remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a lipid-mediated paracrine signaling axis through which tumor-associated microglia/macrophages promote glioma invasion. Integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial lipidomics, and functional perturbation across mouse models and human GBM samples, we show that invading tumor cells engage and reprogram myeloid cells via colony-stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF1R)-PI3K signaling. This induces lipid metabolic reprogramming and secretion of bioactive lipids, including lysophosphatidylcholines (LPCs) and lysophosphatidic acids (LPAs), which promote GBM invasion through distinct downstream pathways. Disruption of this myeloid-GBM axis reduces lipid secretion and suppresses invasion. Targeting downstream LPA-LPA receptor (LPAR) or YAP/TAZ signaling further constrains invasion in a context-dependent manner. Together, these findings define a lipid-driven circuit linking the tumor microenvironment to glioma invasion and identify strategies to reduce infiltration and improve surgical resection.

papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is a modifiable determinant of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), positioning antibiotic exposure as a critical yet under-recognized risk factor for worse survival outcomes in immuno-oncology. As nearly 30% of ICI-treated patients receive antibiotics and indications of cancer immunotherapy are expanding, this issue represents a global challenge in oncology. Here, we paint an updated and comprehensive landscape of antibiotic exposure in immuno-oncology, provide actionable clinical recommendations, and envision future avenues for improvement. First, we describe the biological mechanisms by which antibiotic-induced dysbiosis contributes to ICI resistance. Next, through an updated meta-analysis of 116 cohorts and 97,850 cancer patients treated with ICI, we found a significant association between antibiotic exposure and survival outcomes (overall survival, hazard ratio [HR]: 1.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.34-1.65; progression-free survival, HR: 1.44, 95% CI: 1.31-1.58). Finally, we discuss antibiotics stewardship and microbiome-centered strategies to prevent, diagnose, and/or repair dysbiosis.

papers.abstract: Ocean acidification, characterized by a gradual seawater pH decline, influences marine primary producers such as diatoms, which contribute substantially to oceanic carbon fixation. Experimental studies aiming to project climate change impacts often simulate acidification via abrupt pH shifts, potentially misrepresenting ecological and evolutionary responses. Here we conduct a long-term evolution experiment with the marine diatom Chaetoceros muelleri, comparing abrupt and gradual CO2 increases from 440 to 1000 ppm over 1100 generations. Integrating evolutionary genomics, physiological assays, elemental stoichiometry, and Earth System Modeling, we find that abrupt acidification exaggerates diatom growth and carbon fixation responses by up to 15%, driven by enhanced divergent genomic signals and persistent gene expression changes. Gradual acidification elicits weaker phenotypic and genomic shifts, aligning more closely with natural ocean conditions. These findings suggest that models based on abrupt CO2 increases may overestimate the contribution of Chaetoceros muelleri and maybe also other diatoms to productivity and biogeochemical cycling under ocean acidification, highlighting the importance of gradual pH decline in experimental designs to accurately predict marine ecosystem responses.

papers.abstract: Optical control of magnetization is often symmetry-forbidden because electric fields and magnetization transform differently under inversion and time-reversal. However, through even-order nonlinear response, optical excitation can generate a nonequilibrium magnetic density (the nonlinear Edelstein effect) that acts as an internal Edelstein-Zeeman field coupling to slower magnetic degrees of freedom. Here we demonstrate non-thermal, ultrafast optical control of ferromagnetism in the centrosymmetric van der Waals semiconductor Cr2Ge2Te6 via a resonant nonlinear Edelstein effect. Using time-domain THz emission spectroscopy under near-infrared excitation, we directly observe magnetic dipole radiation arising from optically driven magnetization dynamics. The polarization, fluence, and temperature dependences of the THz emission are quantitatively captured by a mean-field description of a weakly anisotropic Heisenberg ferromagnet subject to an Edelstein-Zeeman field. Our results establish a general nonequilibrium route to optical control of magnetism in centrosymmetric materials.

papers.abstract: Despite progress on noble-metal high-entropy alloy catalysts, noble-metal-free high-entropy alloy catalysts continue to face limitations in activity and stability. Atomic defect engineering holds promise for unlocking catalytic potential, yet efficient strategies for designing defects to simultaneously tailor electronic structures and enhance catalytic active sites in noble-metal-free high-entropy alloys remain challenging. Here, we report a general rule to drive twin formation via precisely tuning lattice strain in metallic nanomaterials. By modeling twin formation energy as a descriptor and employing a gradient-radius hetero-atomic doping strategy, we derive a generalized lattice strain-twin formation energy function that determines critical strain for twinning propensity. Guided by this principle, Ce is incorporated into CuCoNiMnMo nanoparticles, promoting coherent five-fold twinning along {111} planes. Twin boundaries generate high-activity sites by disrupting atomic symmetry and reducing coordination numbers, while modulating band width via altered orbital overlap. Meanwhile, strong Ce-O affinity forms an amorphous CeOx passivation layer on twinned noble-metal-free high-entropy alloy, triggering hetero-interfacial electron transfer. These effects synergistically optimize reaction kinetics. Consequently, the engineered catalyst achieves a 405-cycle lifespan in lithium-oxygen batteries and operates across -20 to 80 °C. Our study brings fundamental insights into defect engineering for electrocatalysis in energy conversion fields.

papers.abstract: Learning to link sensory information to motor actions requires coordinated activity across the cerebral cortex, but how different cortical layers contribute to learning remains unclear. Here we show that learning engages distinct, layer-specific activity patterns across the cortex of male mice during acquisition of a whisker-based go/no-go task. Using wide-field calcium imaging of either layer 2/3 or layer 5 neurons across 25 cortical areas, we found that learning produced markedly different, and sometimes opposing, changes in activity between layers. Layer 5 exhibited widespread suppression before sensory input and enhanced activity in frontal cortex during sensorimotor transformation, whereas layer 2/3 showed learning-related enhancements in higher-order sensory areas during sensation. In contrast, both layers displayed similar learning-related enhancement in barrel cortex during whisker touch. These findings reveal complementary roles of superficial and deep cortical layers during learning and demonstrate that layer-specific cortical dynamics are a fundamental feature of sensorimotor learning.

papers.abstract: Diet is associated with biological aging, yet few existing dietary indices have been developed specifically to target biological aging. We develop a data-driven, food-based Empirical Dietary Index for Slower Epigenetic Aging (EDISEA) to identify dietary features predictive of lower GrimAge2 acceleration. Higher EDISEA is associated with 4.17 years slower epigenetic aging in the derivation sample of 1,711 participants (P-value < 0.001) and 3.77 years slower aging in an independent sample of 2,311 participants. Higher EDISEA is consistently associated with lower all-cause mortality (pooled hazard ratio = 0.80, 95% CI 0.76, 0.85) in two US cohorts, and with lower risks of aging-related diseases, functional limitations, and multimorbidity across US and UK aging cohorts. Outcome-wide analyses in a large UK population-based cohort further show broad health associations, supported by molecular and neuroimaging signatures of more favourable vascular, inflammatory, metabolic, and brain structural profiles. EDISEA may provide an epigenetic aging-informed framework for studying dietary strategies relevant to healthy aging.

papers.abstract: Phosphorylation plays a central role in coordinating transcription with pre-mRNA maturation, yet the mechanistic understanding of how transcription is regulated by phosphorylation remains limited. The PP1 phosphatase removes Cdk9-dependent phosphorylation of Pol II and Spt5, triggering transcription termination. Here, we demonstrate that PNUTS enhances PP1 activity, whereas WDR82 mediates an interaction between PP1 and the pre-mRNA 3'-end processing machinery subunit Symplekin. We present the structure of a PNUTS-WDR82-Symplekin-Ssu72 complex, revealing that PNUTS and Symplekin bind WDR82 through distinct interfaces using conserved short linear motifs. Mutations that inactivate PP1's catalytic activity or disrupt its interaction with either PNUTS or the 3'-end processing machinery led to impaired transcription elongation, inefficient cleavage of nascent transcripts, altered poly(A) site selection, and widespread transcription termination defects. Our findings demonstrate that the PP1 complex is essential for coupling transcription to pre-mRNA 3'-end maturation, ensuring production of functional mRNA.

papers.abstract: Aerogel fibers have many advantages for personal thermal management because of their three-dimensional porous structures, high porosity, thermal insulation, and effective passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) capabilities. However, the porous structure of aerogel fibers significantly weakens their mechanical strength, thereby reducing their cooling efficiency. Here, we develop a method for the continuous production of radially gradient porous bacterial cellulose (BC) aerogel fibers (GP-BCAFs) fabrics. The multilevel gradient micro- and nano-porous structures of the GP-BCAFs provide a high solar reflectivity, while the nano-entangled networks and distinctive wrinkled pores improve their mechanical properties by dissipating stress. The designed structure achieves a balance between strong mechanical properties and cooling performance. The GP-BCAF fabrics exhibit a high mechanical and PDRC performance, including a tensile strength of 50 MPa, a solar reflectivity of 94.7%, a mid-infrared (MIR) emissivity of 97.3%, and an outdoor cooling performance with 8.5 °C temperature lower than that of commercial cotton fabrics. Moreover, a self-powered sensor is built using the GP-BCAF fabric, and its electrical signals allow real-time monitoring of human physiological activities. This work provides a universal, sustainable, and scalable approach to producing PDRC aerogel fibers and multifunctional textiles for outdoor personal thermal management.

papers.abstract: Previous studies have shown that signal regulatory protein γ (SIRPγ) is an important regulatory factor for T cell function. However, its expression and biological role in tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remain unknown. In this study, we find that the level of SIRPγ is significantly upregulated in TPE compared to non-TPE. Furthermore, we demonstrate SIRPγ involvement in TPE pathogenesis through the induction of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, SIRPγ interacts with CD47 to activate the phosphatidylinositol 3/kinase-protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway, leading to the upregulation of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) and the enhancement of serine metabolism. Serine, in turn, facilitates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) epigenetic modification at the NFATC2 locus. This modification, in coordination with TCR-induced calcium signaling, promotes NFATC2 activation, ultimately driving the expression of exhaustion-associated transcription factors and immunosuppressive receptors. Together, our findings identify SIRPγ as a regulator of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion in TPE and suggest its potential as a predictive biomarker for TPE diagnosis.

papers.abstract: While microglia are well known for pruning synapses during neurodevelopment, their role in synapse formation remains understudied. Here we investigate how microglial absence impacts synaptic development in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), a region critical for emotional regulation and motivated behaviors. Using genetically modified mice lacking microglia (Csf1rΔFIRE/ΔFIRE), we find blunted excitatory synapse formation in the NAc, particularly during the second and third postnatal weeks. Tissue-level NAc proteomics in the third postnatal week reveals changes in proteins involved in synapse structure, trans-synaptic signaling, and pre-synaptic function. Although electrophysiological changes largely resolve by adulthood, microglia-lacking mice exhibit persistent changes in threat avoidance behavior and underlying NAc neuronal activity. Transient depletion of NAc microglia during the second postnatal week similarly disrupts synapse formation and adult threat avoidance. Together, these findings identify a role for microglia in shaping NAc synaptic development and in establishing functional circuits that support adult behavioral function.

papers.abstract: With the miniaturization and high integration of microelectronic devices, efficient thermal management is increasingly critical. Conventional thermal interface materials often suffer from a certain degree of mismatch between their thermal conductivity and contact thermal resistance. Herein, we develop a thermal interface fluorofluidic-gel with a branched-type nanocluster-junction network. Benefiting from the interfacial infiltration enabled by the branched-junction fluoronetwork and the efficient thermal pathways constructed by thermal conductive nanocomposites, the fluorofluidic-gel exhibits a high thermal conductivity of 5.89 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ and a low contact thermal resistance of 0.15 cm²·K·W⁻¹. It also achieves reversible adhesion and mechanical resistance, with an adhesive strength of 189.3 kPa, adhesion energy of 220.3 J·m⁻² and impact resistance of 3.91 J·cm⁻¹. In addition, this gel maintains thermal stability from -80 °C to 300 °C and exhibits an electrical breakdown strength exceeding 24 kV/mm. We ‌anticipate‌ that adaptive thermal interface fluorofluidic-gel presents a promising solution for high-heat-flux electronic thermal management.

papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections are a global threat, yet their long-term pathogen-specific mortality dynamics and pandemic-era deviations remain unclear. In this secondary modelling analysis, we evaluate associated mortality under a no-infection counterfactual and attributable mortality under a drug-susceptible infection counterfactual for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections overall and across seven constituent pathogen groups in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Using age-period-cohort decomposition and Bayesian counterfactual modelling, we estimate 1.03 million associated (95% uncertainty interval, 0.90-1.17 million) and 0.22 million attributable (0.17-0.27 million) deaths from these infections in 2021. From 1990 to 2019, overall associated and attributable mortality rates increased by 0.82% (95% confidence interval, 0.77-0.87) and 0.90% (0.85-0.95) per year, respectively. South Asia has the fastest-rising associated and attributable mortality, whereas high-income regions decline. Among constituent pathogens, Klebsiella pneumoniae shows the fastest increase in mortality rates, while Pseudomonas aeruginosa shows declining associated but slightly rising attributable mortality. During 2020-2021, overall associated mortality falls 4.71% below pre-pandemic counterfactual projections, whereas attributable mortality does not change significantly. Here, we show divergent mortality trajectories by region, pathogen, and metric, motivating targeted, dual-metric surveillance and intervention strategies.

papers.title: Global spatiotemporal dynamics of mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections over the past three decades.

papers.abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the DRC and Uganda raises urgent questions about the efficacy of existing Ebola virus (EBOV) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). Here, we perform genomic and structural analyses of 44 BDBV sequences, including 12 from the 2026 outbreak, to assess mAb binding to the viral glycoprotein (GP). While the MBP134 cocktail epitopes remain conserved, mAb114 (Ebanga) binding is compromised by E112D and P116A mutations, causing off-target binding and reduced affinity. Structural modeling of Inmazeb shows that while Odesivimab maintains epitope binding, Atoltivimab and Maftivimab fail to bind their designated sites individually, though the complete trimeric cocktail demonstrates BDBV synergistic binding. These computational models predict mAb114 efficacy against BDBV may be compromised due to epitope mutations affecting binding affinity, whereas MBP134 retains conserved targeting and holds promise as a broadly protective therapeutic. The complex binding behavior of Inmazeb components points to the importance of antibody combinatorial effects for treatment efficacy. These observations warrant urgent experimental validation through neutralization assays.

papers.abstract: Understanding tissue function requires connecting spatial cellular context with molecular depth, yet such integration remains challenging in complex organs like the pancreas. We develop multiplexed Deep Visual Proteomics (mxDVP), an end-to-end workflow combining high-plex imaging, automated computational analysis, and spatially guided ultra-sensitive mass spectrometry. Powered by PIPΣX, an open-source image analysis framework enabling whole-slide membrane-aware segmentation, annotation, and laser microdissection export, mxDVP achieves >6000 protein identifications from as few as 100 small islet cells. Applied to human pancreatic islets, mxDVP segments over 860,000 cells and resolves twelve endocrine subtypes, including rare polyhormonal and intermediate-state populations that exhibit spatial organization patterns, co-expression of INSM1 and SCG3, and hybrid α/β/δ signatures. These findings reveal a spectrum of endocrine heterogeneity and spatial organization. By integrating imaging and deep proteomics in an accessible framework, mxDVP enables discovery of rare cell states whose biological roles depend on tissue architecture.

papers.abstract: Integrating sensing into communication is crucial for the fully-connected and intelligent development of modern life. However, existing fiber-optic sensing and communication systems merely coexist without inadequate resource sharing, resulting in limited scalability for large-scale deployment. Here, we propose a holistically co-designed sensing and communication (CSAC) framework that incorporates multi-level optimization: (i) a dual-function pilot signal that shares time and spectrum resources; (ii) a simplified system using a single transmitter to simultaneously generate multi-tone pilot and subcarrier communication signals; (iii) a point-to-multipoint (P2MP) network that distributes pilot signals for multi-user frequency synchronization and enhanced acoustic sensing response. Our approach achieves multi-point frequency synchronization with an accuracy of 1.56 MHz and enhances acoustic sensing response to 12 kHz. By introducing the on-chip modulators to generate multi-frequency optical comb, the response bandwidth is further expanded to 28 kHz. This CSAC framework efficiently supports dense communication and diverse sensing, offering an eco-sustainable solution for the future optical networks.

papers.abstract: For advanced EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKI) therapy is the primary treatment, but drug resistance and side effects reduce its effectiveness. Integrating Chinese and Western medicine is a key focus in cancer treatment. This study evaluates the clinical benefits of combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with EGFR-TKI, summarizing TCM syndromes and medication traits. We searched six databases for relevant clinical studies. A meta-analysis assessed progression-free survival (PFS), disease control rate (DCR), and adverse reactions, with subgroup analysis by EGFR mutation type. A TCM syndrome network was created to examine syndrome distribution and core prescription patterns. TCM combined with EGFR-TKIs significantly improved PFS (HR = 0.70, 95%CI 0.65-0.76, p < 0.00001, I² = 0%), benefiting patients with Exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation equally (p = 0.75). The combination therapy increased DCR (RR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.01-1.40, p = 0.04), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 89%), and reduced targeted-agent-related adverse reactions. Qi-Yin and Lung-Spleen deficiency were the dominant TCM syndromes, managed via Qi-tonifying, Yin-nourishing and spleen-strengthening regimens. Integrating TCM with EGFR-TKI enhances tumor control and treatment safety in advanced NSCLC patients with EGFR mutations, showing consistent efficacy across various mutation types. This approach, which considers clinical syndrome differentiation and medication patterns in Chinese medicine, offers evidence-based guidance for personalized treatment. This review was performed following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261398486, identifier CRD420261398486.

papers.abstract: The introduction of volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) has enabled dosimetric improvements during prostate bed (PB) radiotherapy; however, the planning target volume (PTV) margins remain substantially greater than for prostate radiotherapy. New approaches are required to further optimise rectal dose and minimise target and organ motion. ProSpare®, a self-inserted rectal obturator designed to facilitate daily image guidance, may enhance radiotherapy accuracy and reduce treatment-related morbidity. Patients scheduled to receive adjuvant or salvage PB radiotherapy after radical prostatectomy were randomised to either standard-of-care (SOC) PB-IMRT using centre-standard PTV margins and verification protocol (SOC) or PB-IMRT with daily ProSpare®-guided radiotherapy using a reduced 5-mm posterior margin. Dose and fractionation schedules were selected by each centre according to protocol recommendations. The primary endpoint is patient-reported EPIC bowel function and bother at 2 years. Secondary endpoints include acute Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) and CTCAE toxicity, patient-reported outcomes, device tolerability, and anorectal dosimetry. We report the results from the prespecified analysis of these secondary endpoints. Between 2017 and 2023, 162 patients were recruited; 158 began radiotherapy and were evaluable at 18 weeks. Acute toxicity data were available for 146 patients (SOC 76/81, ProSpare 70/77). Compared with SOC, ProSpare® was associated with lower 18-week RTOG ≥grade 1 gastrointestinal (GI) and genitourinary (GU) toxicity (39% vs. 31% and 37% vs. 29%, respectively). The incidence of worst CTCAE grade 2 GI and GU toxicity was <6%. Of 51 responders, 50 found ProSpare® tolerable and would recommend its use. Use of ProSpare® resulted in consistently lower ano-rectal dose-volume parameters. ProSpare®-guided prostate bed radiotherapy (PBRT) resulted in lower acute RTOG bowel toxicity at all time points. Patient-reported tolerability was very favourable. Use of ProSpare® improved rectal and anal canal dosimetry. ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT02978014.

papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, and most patients present with unresectable or metastatic disease. In recent years, approaches such as locoregional therapy, immunotherapy and targeted therapy have achieved significant breakthroughs in the transformation treatment of advanced iCCA. We report a case of successful conversion therapy using envafolimab plus olaparib combined with locoregional therapies in advanced iCCA. A 65-year-old male with obstructive jaundice was diagnosed with metastatic iCCA (cT3N1M1, Stage IV) harboring a 117 mm left hepatic lobe lesion, with enlarged lymph nodes, and pulmonary nodules suspicious for metastasis. Next-generation sequencing revealed MSI-H and TMB-H status, along with DDR gene alterations (CDK12 and HDAC2). He received multimodal treatment comprising TACE, HAIC, PD-L1 blockade (envafolimab), and exploratory PARP inhibition (olaparib). Over 20 months, the primary lesion shrank from 117 mm to 42 mm, with regression of lymph nodules and pulmonary nodules and normalization of CA19-9. He underwent R0 resection and pathological examination confirmed a pathological complete response (pCR/ypT0N0) in the resected specimens. At the last follow-up (October 15, 2025), the patient had achieved a progression-free survival of 36 months and a postoperative recurrence-free survival of 16 months. This case demonstrates that the TACE plus HAIC combined with PD-L1 blockade and exploratory PARP inhibition is a promising conversion therapy strategy. It provides preliminary evidence for PARP inhibitor therapy in DDR-altered cholangiocarcinoma, supporting further investigation in prospective trials.

papers.abstract: Previous studies have identified an association between a tumor microenvironment characterized by a predominance of T helper cell type 2 (Th2) system cells (Th2 cells, M2 macrophages, innate lymphoid cells type 2), regulatory T cells, and myeloid derived suppressor cells with poorer cancer prognosis. In contrast, a tumor microenvironment characterized by Th1 system cells (Th1 cells, M1 macrophages, natural killer cells, CD8+ cells, innate lymphoid cells type 1) is associated with a more favorable prognosis. T2-high asthma, a quintessential Th2-dominance-based disease, is associated epidemiologically with more than double the incidence of lung, breast, prostate, and colon cancers, suggesting a connection between the Th2 immune dominant patient macroenvironment and the Th2 immune dominant tumor microenvironment. Stress, air pollution, toxicants, sleep disruption, obesity, and many other influences from the exposome are known to drive the patient into Th2 dominance. Thus, the authors hypothesize that there is a through-line connecting the exposome, patient macroenvironment, and tumor microenvironment. With this context in mind, specific defects in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle produce oncometabolites that drive oncogenic development in tissues. However these same TCA cycle defects drive macrophages to the M1 phenotype, which activates the Th1 system. Th1 system cells are responsible for clearance of oncogenically transformed cells. This should represent a check against the oncogenic influence of the oncometabolites created by the TCA cycle breaks. The authors hypothesize that, in Th2 dominant patients, the TCA cycle breaks fail to shift macrophages to the M1 phenotype, the Th1 system fails to upregulate, and the normal check against oncogenic development fails to occur. If confirmed by subsequent studies, this model may help explain the more than doubled incidence of common cancers in asthma and potentially other Th2 atopic diseases. The authors discuss clinical implications and approaches for operationalizing existing knowledge of the exposome and its impact on patient immunology.

papers.abstract: Colorectal adenomas (CRAs) are the primary precancerous lesions in the development of colorectal cancer; establishing a simple, cost-effective and non-invasive tool for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy is of great significance for risk stratification. To investigate the association between peripheral blood metabolic and inflammatory markers and the risk of colorectal adenomas, and to develop a personalised risk prediction model for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy. This study was a single-centre retrospective case-control study conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of Shandong Second Medical University. The study included 2,437 patients with colorectal polyps who underwent endoscopic resection between January 2020 and December 2025. Demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors and peripheral blood biochemical markers, with a particular focus on the triglyceride-to-glucose (TyG) ratio and markers of systemic inflammation. Patients with colorectal adenomas confirmed by histopathology. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The study included 2,437 participants (mean age 58.57 years; 1,323 men [54.29%]), patients in the adenoma group (n=1,584) were significantly older and had a higher proportion of men compared with the control group (n=853). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that male sex (OR, 1.621; 95% CI, 1.269-2.074), age ≥56.5 years (OR, 1.868; 95% CI, 1.515-2.205) and a TyG index ≥8.562 (OR, 1.271; 95% CI, 1.015-1.590) were independent risk factors for the development of colorectal adenomas. The AUC of this predictive model was 0.631 and 0.607 in the training and validation sets, respectively, indicates moderate discriminatory power. The model is well calibrated; analysis of the decision curve shows that, across a range of threshold probabilities, the model yields a positive net benefit compared with strategies involving either universal treatment or universal non-treatment. The findings suggest that male gender, advanced age and an elevated TyG index are independently associated with the risk of colorectal adenomas. The non-invasive nomogram developed in this study provides a simple risk stratification tool to aid in distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy.

papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent extracranial solid malignant tumor in infants and children. Approximately half of children with high-risk NB exhibit primary resistance to first-line therapy or experience disease relapse within two years post-treatment, leading to dismal overall survival. PANoptosis is an inflammatory programmed cell death modality integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis and necroptosis; nevertheless, the functional relevance of PANoptosis-related genes (PRGs) in NB remains largely undefined. This study aimed to explore PRGs associated with NB prognosis and their link to the tumor immune microenvironment, so as to identify novel therapeutic targets for NB. mRNA expression profiles from three public NB datasets (GSE49711-NB, TARGET-NB and E-MTAB-8248-NB) were used to investigate the prognostic roles of 19 previously reported PRGs. Independent Cox regression screening was performed in each cohort to identify cohort-specific prognostic PRGs, followed by Venn intersection analysis to identify conserved prognostic genes. PARP1 expression was validated in tumor tissues from 127 clinical NB patients. The GIS score based on PARP1 expression and clinical metadata were combined to assess its prognostic value. In vitro functional assays were performed to explore the anti-tumor effects and mechanisms of the PARP1 inhibitor AZD5305. Venn intersection analysis identified PARP1 as the only shared gene with consistent prognostic significance across heterogeneous NB patient populations. In vitro experiments revealed that AZD5305 markedly suppressed NB cell proliferation, migration and invasion, triggered cell apoptosis, and arrested cell cycle progression at the G0/G1 phase. This study adopts a multi-cohort parallel screening strategy to mine conserved therapeutic targets for NB. Our data indicate that PARP1 inhibition via AZD5305 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for NB treatment.

papers.abstract: This study, through a meta-analysis, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from database inception to January 13, 2026. EndNote 21was employed for literature screening and data extraction. Meta-analysis was carried out on the extracted data using Stata 15, MetaDisc 1.4, and MedCalc. In total, 21 studies were included, involving 2,023 patients with HCC, of whom 890 were MVI+ and 1,133 were MVI-. In univariable analyses, both tumor-to-normal liver uptake ratio (TLR) (odds ratio [OR] = 2.577, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.446-4.593, P = 0.001) and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (OR = 1.272, 95% CI: 1.036-1.561, P = 0.021) were significantly associated with an increased MVI risk. After multivariable adjustment, SUVmax retained independent predictive value (OR = 2.140, 95% CI: 1.244-3.681, P = 0.006), whereas the multivariable evidence for TLR was derived from a single study and required further validation. AUC values for SUVmax and radiomics score (Rad-score) were 0.819 (95% CI: 0.739-0.899) and 0.809 (95% CI: 0.762-0.857), respectively, with relatively balanced values for sensitivity, specificity, and negative likelihood ratio. The available evidence supports SUVmax as one of the metabolic markers for preoperative MVI risk assessment in HCC, with Rad-score similar to SUVmax in diagnostic discrimination. The complementary value of the two markers was not demonstrated by this Meta-analysis, but rather derived from inferences proposed by external studies. Moreover, because the included radiomics studies did not report a pooled effect size for the combined model integrating SUVmax and Rad-score, a Meta-analysis targeting this model is currently not feasible. Therefore, the complementarity of SUVmax and Rad-score should be regarded as a hypothesis to be tested. In the future, multicenter, prospective radiomics studies with rigorous external validation are warranted to further explore a combined prediction model based on SUVmax and Rad-score. On this basis, an integrated assessment workflow should be gradually established, by which preoperative decisions are guided. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261289724.

papers.abstract: Obesity increases the risk and progression of at least 13 types of cancer. Although the epidemiologic links between excess adiposity and these cancers are well documented, the biological mechanisms linking obesity to carcinogenesis and tumor progression remain incompletely understood. White adipose tissue in obesity is a source of inflammatory and immunosuppressive signals that act systemically, driving metabolic, inflammatory, and immune dysfunction whose consequences differ across tumor types. As adipose tissue expands and adipocytes enlarge, the blood supply becomes inadequate, leading to hypoxia, fibrosis, lipolytic stress, macrophage recruitment, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These obesity-induced perturbations generate endocrine, cytokine, lipid, and metabolic signals that act systemically, within the tumor microenvironment (TME), and/or cell-intrinsically to activate oncogenic and tumor-promoting pathways. The same signals reshape innate and adaptive immunity, promoting tumor-permissive macrophage states and myeloid-derived suppressor cell expansion, while the effector arms weaken as antigen presentation, natural killer cell and T cell function all decline. This review synthesizes current evidence linking obesity-associated inflammation and immune dysregulation to cancer initiation, progression, and treatment responses across multiple obesity-related cancers. Emphasis is placed on adipose tissue inflammation, myeloid cell biology, T cell immunometabolism, endocrine-inflammatory crosstalk, and the relationship between obesity and immunotherapy. Finally, we discuss translational opportunities for preventing or intercepting obesity-related cancers, including weight loss achieved through lifestyle, surgical, or pharmacologic approaches, with an emphasis on GLP-1 receptor agonists given their substantial efficacy, rapid clinical uptake, and potential to reshape obesity-related cancer prevention and survivorship strategies. Defining the metabolic, immune, and inflammatory phenotypes that drive obesity-associated cancer risk and progression will be essential for developing more precise, mechanism-based strategies for prevention, treatment, and survivorship care.

papers.abstract: Engineered microbial immunotherapies can localize immune-modulating signals within solid tumors, where hypoxia, suppressive myeloid cells, deficient antigen presentation, and dysfunctional T-cell trafficking often limit immunotherapy. Macrofungal polysaccharides, especially structurally defined β-glucans, offer mechanistic templates rather than interchangeable drug substances for source-specific, structure-controlled immune engineering programs. Their activity depends on linkage, branching, molecular mass, conformation, solubility, aggregation, and physical presentation. Critically, the strongest Dectin-1 and trained-immunity evidence discussed here uses particulate β-glucans from Saccharomyces cerevisiae; those findings cannot be assigned directly to macrofungal β-glucans without material-specific comparison. We therefore distinguish four engineering architectures: de novo microbial biosynthesis of a defined β-glucan, microbial surface display, delivery of a pre-characterized β-glucan cargo, and delivery of non-glycan payloads that mimic the desired downstream immune program. Because therapeutic bacteria have not yet been shown to reproduce a macrofungal β-glucan with controlled linkage, branching, conformation, and presentation, near-term development should prioritize standardized cargo delivery or pathway mimicry. In pancreatic and colorectal cancer models, yeast whole-glucan particles have altered myeloid trafficking or generated epigenetically and metabolically trained macrophages linked to CXCL9/CXCL10 production, natural killer-cell recruitment, conventional type 1 dendritic-cell accumulation, and stronger CD8 T-cell responses. Human evidence remains preliminary and cannot establish β-glucan-specific efficacy in uncontrolled combination studies. This Perspective proposes source-resolved material characterization, receptor and cell-state testing, multidimensional pharmacodynamic biomarkers, and microbial safety controls as prerequisites for translating fungal-inspired immune programs into precision cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: From macrofungal polysaccharides to precision microbial immunotherapy: reprogramming the tumor microenvironment through immunometabolic and gene-regulatory pathways.

papers.abstract: Clinically node-negative (cN0) breast cancer accounts for a large proportion of newly diagnosed cases, and its axillary management is undergoing a paradigm shift toward de-escalation aimed at minimizing surgical morbidity. Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) has replaced axillary lymph node dissection (ALND) for nodal staging in cN0 disease, and subsequent trials have questioned the need for completion ALND in selected SLN-positive patients. This narrative review summarizes two decades of pivotal trial evidence across three conceptually distinct de-escalation strategies, which differ in their levels of evidence. First, phase III randomized evidence supports omission of ALND after a positive SLNB for isolated tumor cells and micrometastases (IBCSG 23-01; 10-year disease-free survival HR 0.85, with the non-inferiority criterion met), and for 1-2 macrometastases when combined with breast-conserving surgery and radiotherapy (ACOSOG Z0011, AMAROS, SENOMAC). Second, omission of SLNB itself has demonstrated 5-year oncological safety in rigorously selected low-risk patients with small tumors and negative preoperative axillary ultrasonography (SOUND, INSEMA), in cohorts that were predominantly HR-positive/HER2-negative. Third, emerging strategies, such as advanced imaging, ctDNA-based monitoring, and AI-assisted diagnostics, may further refine patient selection but remain investigational and are not part of established clinical practice at present. The current evidence is insufficient to support routine de-escalation in HER2-positive and triple-negative disease or in other populations underrepresented in the pivotal trials. Axillary de-escalation is therefore justified only within the specific clinical scenarios validated by randomized trials, and aggressive subtypes and biomarker-guided strategies require further prospective evidence before integration into clinical practice.
